88	/****************************************************************************
89	 * Private Types
90	 ****************************************************************************/
91	
92	struct bk7258_wdt_lowerhalf_s
93	{
94	  struct watchdog_lowerhalf_s wdt_lh;  /* Must be first */
95	  uint32_t timeout;                    /* Current timeout in ms */
96	  bool     started;                    /* WDT is armed */
97	};
98	
99	/****************************************************************************
100	 * Private Function Prototypes
101	 ****************************************************************************/
102	
103	static int bk7258_wdt_start(struct watchdog_lowerhalf_s *lower);
104	static int bk7258_wdt_stop(struct watchdog_lowerhalf_s *lower);
105	static int bk7258_wdt_keepalive(struct watchdog_lowerhalf_s *lower);
106	static int bk7258_wdt_getstatus(struct watchdog_lowerhalf_s *lower,
107	                                struct watchdog_status_s *status);
108	static int bk7258_wdt_settimeout(struct watchdog_lowerhalf_s *lower,
109	                                 uint32_t timeout);
110	
111	/****************************************************************************
112	 * Private Data
113	 ****************************************************************************/
114	
115	static const struct watchdog_ops_s g_bk7258_wdt_ops =
116	{
117	  .start      = bk7258_wdt_start,
118	  .stop       = bk7258_wdt_stop,
119	  .keepalive  = bk7258_wdt_keepalive,
120	  .getstatus  = bk7258_wdt_getstatus,
121	  .settimeout = bk7258_wdt_settimeout,
122	};
123	
124	static struct bk7258_wdt_lowerhalf_s g_bk7258_wdt;
125	
126	/****************************************************************************
127	 * Private Helpers
128	 ****************************************************************************/
129	
130	/* Write the two-step key sequence to WDT_CTRL (mirrors wdt_ll_set_period).
131	 * The first write with key1 unlocks; the second with key2 applies the period. */
132	
133	static inline void bk7258_wdt_write_period(uint32_t period)
134	{
135	  putreg32((BK7258_WDT_KEY1 << BK7258_WDT_KEY_SHIFT) |
136	           (period & BK7258_WDT_PERIOD_MASK),
137	           BK7258_WDT_CTRL);
138	
139	  putreg32((BK7258_WDT_KEY2 << BK7258_WDT_KEY_SHIFT) |
140	           (period & BK7258_WDT_PERIOD_MASK),
141	           BK7258_WDT_CTRL);
142	}
143	
144	/****************************************************************************
145	 * Private: lower-half operations
146	 ****************************************************************************/
147	
148	static int bk7258_wdt_start(struct watchdog_lowerhalf_s *lower)
149	{
150	  struct bk7258_wdt_lowerhalf_s *priv =
151	    (struct bk7258_wdt_lowerhalf_s *)lower;
152	
153	  /* Ensure SYS_CTRL WDT config (bootloader already did this, but be
154	   * defensive: if NuttX is entered via a path that skipped the bootloader,
155	   * the WDT clock might not be configured). */
156	
157	  uint32_t v = getreg32(BK7258_SYS_CTRL_REG);
158	  v = (v & ~BK7258_WDT_SYSCTRL_MASK) | BK7258_WDT_SYSCTRL_VAL;
159	  putreg32(v, BK7258_SYS_CTRL_REG);
160	
161	  /* Soft-reset the WDT state machine (mirrors wdt_ll_set_period). */
162	
163	  putreg32(1u, BK7258_WDT_GLOBAL_CTRL);
164	
165	  /* Arm the WDT with the configured period. */
166	
167	  bk7258_wdt_write_period(priv->timeout);
168	
169	  priv->started = true;
170	  wdinfo("started, timeout=%" PRIu32 " ms\n", priv->timeout);
171	  return OK;
172	}
173	
174	static int bk7258_wdt_stop(struct watchdog_lowerhalf_s *lower)
175	{
176	  struct bk7258_wdt_lowerhalf_s *priv =
177	    (struct bk7258_wdt_lowerhalf_s *)lower;
178	
179	  /* Disarm: key sequence with period=0 (mirrors wdt_hal_close for BK7236,
180	   * wdt_hal.c:116-125). */
181	
182	  putreg32(1u, BK7258_WDT_GLOBAL_CTRL);
183	  putreg32(BK7258_WDT_KEY1 << BK7258_WDT_KEY_SHIFT, BK7258_WDT_CTRL);
184	  putreg32(BK7258_WDT_KEY2 << BK7258_WDT_KEY_SHIFT, BK7258_WDT_CTRL);
185	
186	  priv->started = false;
187	  wdinfo("stopped\n");
188	  return OK;
189	}
190	
191	/* keepalive = reinit with same period (SDK bk_wdt_feed = wdt_hal_init_wdt
192	 * with same period, wdt_driver.c:172-180). */
193	
194	static int bk7258_wdt_keepalive(struct watchdog_lowerhalf_s *lower)
195	{
196	  struct bk7258_wdt_lowerhalf_s *priv =
197	    (struct bk7258_wdt_lowerhalf_s *)lower;
198	
199	  /* Feed = clear status + reinit with same period.
200	   * Matches the bootloader's boot_wdt_feed() which works:
201	   *   clear APB_WDT status bit[1:0], then key1+period, key2+period.
202	   * Do NOT soft_reset here — soft_reset may clear the WDT clock gate
203	   * (the SDK's wdt_init_common() re-powers the clock after soft_reset,
204	   * but we don't have that call in keepalive). */
205	
206	  putreg32(getreg32(BK7258_WDT_STATUS) & ~0x3u, BK7258_WDT_STATUS);
207	  bk7258_wdt_write_period(priv->timeout);
208	  return OK;
209	}
210	
211	static int bk7258_wdt_getstatus(struct watchdog_lowerhalf_s *lower,
212	                                struct watchdog_status_s *status)
213	{
214	  struct bk7258_wdt_lowerhalf_s *priv =
215	    (struct bk7258_wdt_lowerhalf_s *)lower;
216	
217	  status->flags = WDFLAGS_RESET;
218	  if (priv->started)
219	    {
220	      status->flags |= WDFLAGS_ACTIVE;
221	    }
222	
223	  status->timeout = priv->timeout;
224	
225	  /* timeleft: we cannot read the current counter from the BK7258 APB WDT
226	   * (no readable counter register).  Return timeout as an upper bound. */
227	
228	  status->timeleft = priv->timeout;
229	  return OK;
230	}
231	
232	static int bk7258_wdt_settimeout(struct watchdog_lowerhalf_s *lower,
233	                                 uint32_t timeout)
234	{
235	  struct bk7258_wdt_lowerhalf_s *priv =
236	    (struct bk7258_wdt_lowerhalf_s *)lower;
237	
238	  if (timeout > BK7258_WDT_PERIOD_MASK)
239	    {
240	      timeout = BK7258_WDT_PERIOD_MASK;
241	    }
242	
243	  priv->timeout = timeout;
244	
245	  /* If already running, re-arm with new period. */
246	
247	  if (priv->started)
248	    {
249	      bk7258_wdt_write_period(priv->timeout);
250	    }
251	
252	  wdinfo("timeout set to %" PRIu32 " ms\n", priv->timeout);
253	  return OK;
254	}

257	 * Public Functions

260	/****************************************************************************
261	 * Name: bk7258_wdt_initialize
262	 *
263	 * Description:
264	 *   Initialize the BK7258 APB WDT and register as /dev/watchdog0.
265	 *   Mirrors the SDK bk_wdt_driver_init + bk_wdt_start path:
266	 *     - Select APB WDT (the bootloader already configured SYS_CTRL and
267	 *       AON/ABP WDT key sequences; we re-assert the config defensively).
268	 *     - Set default period (8 s, matching bootloader WDT_PERIOD).
269	 *     - Register the NuttX watchdog lower-half.
270	 *
271	 *   After registration, opening /dev/watchdog0 and calling start enables
272	 *   CONFIG_WATCHDOG_AUTOMONITOR (if configured), which feeds the WDT
273	 *   automatically via work queue.
274	 *
275	 *   Call this from board_app_initialize() (bk7258_bringup.c), after procfs
276	 *   mount and before DVFS or other long-running init.
277	 *
278	 ****************************************************************************/
279	
280	int bk7258_wdt_initialize(void)
281	{
282	  struct bk7258_wdt_lowerhalf_s *priv = &g_bk7258_wdt;
283	
284	  priv->wdt_lh.ops = &g_bk7258_wdt_ops;
285	  priv->timeout    = BK7258_WDT_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS;
286	  priv->started    = false;
287	
288	  /* The bootloader already armed the WDT (period=8000, SYS_CTRL=0x26).
289	   * We don't re-arm here — start() does that when the upper-half opens
290	   * the device.  This matches the SDK pattern where bk_wdt_driver_init
291	   * does NOT call bk_wdt_start; the caller decides when to arm. */
292	
293	  watchdog_register("/dev/watchdog0",
294	                    (struct watchdog_lowerhalf_s *)priv);
295	
296	  wdinfo("BK7258 WDT registered as /dev/watchdog0, default timeout=%" PRIu32
297	         " ms\n", priv->timeout);
298	  return OK;
299	}
300	
301	#endif /* CONFIG_BK7258_WDT */

1	/*
2	 * boot_wdt.h - BK7258 Tier-1 bootloader WDT (watchdog timer) helpers.
3	 *
4	 * Freestanding (no libc, stack-only, no .bss/.data).  Provides WDT init
5	 * and feed for the product-grade bootloader: if the cold-init DPLL sequence
6	 * or app validation hangs, the WDT resets the chip within ~8 seconds.
7	 *
8	 * Mirrors the Armino SDK WDT unlock/feed protocol (wdt_reg.h, wdt_ll.h,
9	 * wdt_hal.c) and the vendor bootloader's sub_2000FE4 / sub_2001010
10	 * (bk-official-bootloader-reverse.md §2.4).
11	 *
12	 * BK7258 has two watchdogs:
13	 *   APB_WDT @ 0x44800000 (ctrl @ +0x10, status @ +0x04)
14	 *   AON_WDT @ 0x44000600 (ctrl @ +0x00, same key protocol)
15	 *
16	 * ctrl register (wdt_struct.h):
17	 *   period[15:0]  — timeout value (WDT clock ticks; SDK default 8000 ≈ 8s)
18	 *   key[23:16]    — unlock/feed key (0x5A first, 0xA5 second)
19	 *
20	 * Key sequence (two consecutive writes to ctrl):
21	 *   1st write: (0x5A << 16) | period   — unlock
22	 *   2nd write: (0xA5 << 16) | period   — apply (WDT armed)
23	 *
24	 * Feed: clear APB_WDT status bit[1:0], then reinit (same key+period).
25	 */
26	
27	#ifndef __BOOTLOADER_BOOT_WDT_H
28	#define __BOOTLOADER_BOOT_WDT_H
29	
30	#include <stdint.h>
31	
32	/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
33	/* MMIO.                                                              */
34	/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
35	
36	#define REG32(addr)       (*(volatile uint32_t *)(addr))
37	
38	/* SYS block (for SYS_CTRL WDT clock/reset config). */
39	#define SYS_CTRL_REG      0x44000008u
40	
41	/* APB WDT (NMI WDT / main WDT). */
42	#define WDT_APB_BASE      0x44800000u
43	#define WDT_APB_CTRL      (WDT_APB_BASE + 0x10u)   /* period + key */
44	#define WDT_APB_STATUS    (WDT_APB_BASE + 0x04u)   /* status (write 0 to clear bit[1:0]) */
45	
46	/* AON WDT (always-on WDT). */
47	#define WDT_AON_BASE      0x44000600u
48	#define WDT_AON_CTRL      WDT_AON_BASE              /* same ctrl layout */
49	
50	/* Key values (wdt_reg.h:35-36). */
51	#define WDT_KEY1          0x5Au
52	#define WDT_KEY2          0xA5u
53	
54	/* Timeout period.  8000 ≈ 8 seconds (matches SDK CONFIG_INT_WDT_PERIOD_MS).
55	 * The WDT clock is ~1 kHz (ROSC 32 kHz / 32 or similar), so period in
56	 * the register is approximately milliseconds.  8 s covers cold-init
57	 * (worst-case ~100 ms) with 80× margin; a real hang resets in ≤ 8 s. */
58	#define WDT_PERIOD        8000u
59	
60	/* SYS_CTRL bits[5:0] = 0x26: vendor bootloader's WDT clock/reset config
61	 * (bk-official-bootloader-reverse.md §2.4, sub_2000FE4: bic.w r1,r3,#0x3F
62	 * then orr.w ip,r1,#0x26). */
63	#define WDT_SYSCTRL_MASK  0x3Fu
64	#define WDT_SYSCTRL_VAL   0x26u
65	
66	/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
67	/* Public (static inline, stack-only, no libc).                        */
68	/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
69	
70	/* Initialize both WDTs with the vendor key sequence.
71	 * Called once at the start of c_main().  After this, the WDT is armed
72	 * and will reset the chip in ~8 s unless boot_wdt_feed() is called. */
73	static inline void boot_wdt_init(void)
74	{
75	    uint32_t v;
76	    uint32_t ctrl1;
77	    uint32_t ctrl2;
78	
79	    /* 1. SYS_CTRL: configure WDT clock source + reset enable
80	     * (mirrors vendor sub_2000FE4: bic #0x3F, orr #0x26). */
81	    v = REG32(SYS_CTRL_REG);
82	    v = (v & ~WDT_SYSCTRL_MASK) | WDT_SYSCTRL_VAL;
83	    REG32(SYS_CTRL_REG) = v;
84	
85	    ctrl1 = (uint32_t)(WDT_KEY1 << 16) | (WDT_PERIOD & 0xFFFFu);
86	    ctrl2 = (uint32_t)(WDT_KEY2 << 16) | (WDT_PERIOD & 0xFFFFu);
87	
88	    /* 2. Unlock + arm APB_WDT (two-step key). */
89	    REG32(WDT_APB_CTRL) = ctrl1;
90	    REG32(WDT_APB_CTRL) = ctrl2;
91	
92	    /* 3. Unlock + arm AON_WDT (same protocol). */
93	    REG32(WDT_AON_CTRL) = ctrl1;
94	    REG32(WDT_AON_CTRL) = ctrl2;
95	}
96	
97	/* Feed (kick) the WDT.  Clears the APB_WDT status and re-arms with the
98	 * same period, mirroring vendor sub_2001010 (clear status + reinit).
99	 * Call this at key points in c_main to prevent premature reset. */
100	static inline void boot_wdt_feed(void)
101	{
102	    uint32_t ctrl1;
103	    uint32_t ctrl2;
104	
105	    /* Clear APB_WDT status bit[1:0]. */
106	    REG32(WDT_APB_STATUS) = REG32(WDT_APB_STATUS) & ~0x3u;
107	
108	    ctrl1 = (uint32_t)(WDT_KEY1 << 16) | (WDT_PERIOD & 0xFFFFu);
109	    ctrl2 = (uint32_t)(WDT_KEY2 << 16) | (WDT_PERIOD & 0xFFFFu);
110	
111	    /* Re-arm APB_WDT (= feed). */
112	    REG32(WDT_APB_CTRL) = ctrl1;
113	    REG32(WDT_APB_CTRL) = ctrl2;
114	}
115	
116	#endif /* __BOOTLOADER_BOOT_WDT_H */

现在我对问题全貌已经清楚了。让我分析根因。

**问题根因分析：**

BOOT 流程：
1. bootloader `boot_wdt_init()` —— 开 **APB WDT** **和** **AON WDT**，period=8000 (~8s)，都 armed
2. bootloader 跳转到 app
3. app `bk7258_bringup.c` 调 `bk7258_wdt_initialize()` —— **只注册 `/dev/watchdog0`，不喂狗**
4. NuttX `watchdog_register` 只是注册设备，**不喂狗**。要喂狗必须 open `/dev/watchdog0` + `WDIOC_START`

关键问题：

**① AON WDT 从来没人喂。** bootloader 开了 APB + AON 两个 WDT，但 app 侧 `bk7258_wdt.c` 只管 APB WDT (`0x44800000`)，**AON WDT (`0x44000600`) 完全没碰**。AON WDT 仍然 armed，8 秒后必然复位 → app 一直重启。

**② APB WDT 也没人喂。** `bk7258_wdt_initialize()` 注释自己说「不 re-arm，等 upper-half open 后 start」。但 bringup 里只调 `bk7258_wdt_initialize()`，**没有 open `/dev/watchdog0` 也没有调用 start**。除非有进程主动 `open("/dev/watchdog0")` + `ioctl(WDIOC_START)`，否则 `CONFIG_WATCHDOG_AUTOMONITOR` 不会触发喂狗。bootloader 的 APB WDT 8 秒后也会复位。

**③ `CONFIG_WATCHDOG_AUTOMONITOR` 是被动的。** 它只在 `/dev/watchdog0` 被 open 之后才启用工作队列喂狗；没有人 open，就不喂。生产环境要么有 nsh/看门狗守护进程 open 它，要么用 `CONFIG_WATCHDOG_REGISTER` + board 自己主动 start。

**核心修复方向**：app bringup 必须在进 app 后**第一时间**喂掉 bootloader 留下的两条狗（APB + AON），并主动 start APB WDT 让 NuttX automonitor 接管喂狗；AON WDT 要么关掉，要么 app 也保持喂它。

先确认下这两点（AON WDT 基址、defconfig 里 WDT/automonitor 配置），再看 driver-code-reviewer skill 怎么要求：

1. `bk7258_wdt_initialize()` 只注册设备、不 open、不 start → APB WDT 没人喂 → 8s 复位
2. **完全没有 AON WDT 代码** → AON WDT 也没人喂 → 8s 复位

这就是进 app 一直重启的根因。

text:
Base directory for this skill: /home/lijian/project/open-vela/.claude/skills/driver-code-reviewer

# NuttX Driver Code Reviewer

基于 59 Pattern（52 质量 + 7 设计）的驱动代码质量审查，双轮交叉验证 + 量化评分。
**不修改被审查代码**，Critical 问题仅给出修复建议。

完整 Pattern 定义和维度规格见 `references/layer1-code-quality-spec.md`。

## 外部依赖

| 依赖 | 用途 | 缺失时降级方案 |
|------|------|---------------|
| `nuttx-driver-development` skill | 子系统 pattern 参考 | 仅用本 skill 内置规则 |
| `feishu` skill 或 `feishu-mcp` | 飞书报告输出（可选） | 跳过飞书，仅本地报告 |

## 触发格式

```
review <路径>
review <路径>，对比 <分支名>
```

---

## 维度体系

### 质量维度（L1-1 ~ L1-7，参与评分，100 分制）

| 维度 | 分值 | Pattern 数 | 审查内容 |
|------|:----:|:----------:|----------|
| **L1-1 内存安全** | 20 | 8 | 空指针、UAF、double-free、未初始化、堆泄漏 |
| **L1-2 并发安全** | 20 | 7 | 数据竞争、死锁、锁误用、原子性违反 |
| **L1-3 资源管理** | 10 | 7 | fd/sem/timer/work_queue 申请释放配对 |
| **L1-4 错误处理** | 10 | 4 | 返回值检查、错误传播、状态回滚 |
| **L1-5 类型与数值安全** | 10 | 5 | 整数溢出、符号混用、截断、移位 |
| **L1-6 输入与边界校验** | 15 | 12 | 缓冲区边界、ioctl 参数、格式串注入 |
| **L1-7 嵌入式专项** | 15 | 9 | DMA/cache、ISR、RPMSG、W1C 寄存器、PM |

权重分层依据：
- T0 致命（40%）：L1-1 + L1-2 — 直接导致 crash/数据损坏
- T1 严重（30%）：L1-6 + L1-7 — 攻击入口 + RTOS 独有陷阱
- T2 重要（30%）：L1-3 + L1-4 + L1-5 — 长期影响但很少立即致命

### 维度适用性判定

如果驱动不涉及某维度的检查场景，该维度标记为 **N/A**，其分值按比例重分配到其余适用维度。

| 场景 | N/A 维度 | 理由 |
|------|----------|------|
| 纯 I2C 线程驱动，无 ISR/中断 | L1-7 中 P-47/P-49 跳过 | 无中断上下文 |
| 无 DMA/RPMSG/PM 关键词 | L1-7 整体 N/A | 嵌入式专项不适用 |
| 无并发访问（单线程 chardev） | L1-2 中 P-09~P-14 部分跳过 | 无共享状态 |
| 无外部输入（纯硬件寄存器驱动） | L1-6 部分 N/A | 无用户空间输入 |

**权重重分配公式**：N/A 维度的分值按剩余维度原始权重比例分配。例如 L1-7(15分) N/A 时，15 分按 20:20:10:10:10:15 比例分配到 L1-1~L1-6。

### 独立信号（不参与质量评分）

| 维度 | 扣分上限 | Pattern 数 | 审查内容 |
|------|:--------:|:----------:|----------|
| **L1-8 设计哲学** | -10 | 7 | 抽象层绕过、命名空间污染、影子状态、重复造轮子 |
| **需求/设计一致性** | 独立报告 | — | 对照 requirement.md/design.md 检查功能完整性 |

---

## 评分规则

### 严重度与扣分（L1-1 ~ L1-7）

| 严重度 | 扣分 | 定义 |
|--------|:----:|------|
| Critical | -15 | 导致 crash、数据损坏或安全漏洞 |
| High | -8 | 显著影响代码质量，但不一定立即致命 |
| Medium | -3 | 值得修改但不阻塞 |
| Low | -1 | 改进建议 |

### L1-8 设计哲学扣分（独立）

| 严重度 | 扣分 | 适用 Pattern |
|--------|:----:|-------------|
| High | -4 | DP-01 绕过抽象层, DP-02 跨层依赖, DP-05 板级侵入, DP-06 影子状态 |
| Medium | -2 | DP-03 头文件泄漏, DP-04 缺少 static, DP-07 重复造轮子 |

### 置信度体系

| Pattern Confidence | 评分置信度 | 处理方式 |
|:------------------:|:---------:|----------|
| HIGH | 0.8 | 直接扣分 |
| MEDIUM | 0.6 | 扣分 + 标注需人工确认 |
| LOW | 0.4 | 仅 WARNING，不扣分 |

### 计算

```
维度得分 = 满分(含重分配) - Σ(每个 issue 的扣分)，最低 0 分
总分 = Σ(各适用维度得分)（满分 100）
一票否决：任一维度出现 Critical → 总分封顶 60
```

### 结论判定

| 总分 | 条件 | 结论 |
|------|------|------|
| ≥ 80 | 且无 Critical | **PASS** |
| 60-79 | 或有可修复 Critical | **NEEDS_FIX** |
| < 60 | — | **REJECT** |

### 设计健康度（L1-8，独立输出）

```
设计健康度 = 10 - Σ(DP-pattern 扣分)，最低 0
等级：A(8-10) / B(5-7) / C(0-4)
不影响质量总分和结论判定
```

### Step 0: 收集元信息

从本地收集审查目标的元信息（文件列表、对比分支）。
**主流程不获取文件内容** — 文件内容由每个审查 agent 自行获取，保证独立性。

1. `get_change` 获取元信息（status, project, branch, patchset）— 401/403 中断并提示检查凭证

| **NEW/DRAFT** | `get_file_content(branch="refs/changes/XX/<change>/<patchset>")` | XX = change 号末两位，patchset 从 get_files 返回 |

#### API 限流策略

**Round 1**：按 `agents/code-review/prompt.md` 执行 — 52 Pattern 逐项检查（L1-1~L1-7）+ 7 DP-Pattern（L1-8）+ 需求一致性。
**Round 2**：按 `agents/deep-review/prompt.md` 执行 — 侧重内存安全、并发竞态、资源生命周期的深层逻辑分析。

#### 执行模式

**默认模式（并行 subagent，各自获取源码）**：

每个 subagent 在独立上下文中自行读取源码文件并审查。主流程只传递文件路径列表。

主流程 Step 0 收集元信息

**优势**：

- 两个 subagent 完全独立，互不可见

**Subagent prompt 中必须包含**：

# WDT 驱动审查报告

**目标**：`board/bk7258_t5ai/chip/bk7258_wdt.c` / `bk7258_wdt.h`
**参考**：`bootloader/boot_wdt.h`（bootloader 侧）、SDK `aon_wdt_reg.h` / `wdt_reg.h`
**板端症状**：bootloader 开狗 8s，进 app 后 ~8s 复位，无限重启

---

## 根因分析

进 app 无限重启是**两个独立缺陷叠加**导致两条狗都没人喂：

### 缺陷 1（Critical）：AON WDT 完全无处理
`boot_wdt_init()` 同时 arm APB WDT（`0x44800000`）和 AON WDT（`0x44000600`）。但 `bk7258_wdt.c` 全文只引用 `0x44800000`，**AON WDT 基址 `0x44000600` 从未出现**。进 app 后 AON WDT 持续倒计时，无人喂、无人关，~8s 必然复位。

### 缺陷 2（Critical）：APB WDT 没人 start / 喂
`bk7258_wdt_initialize()` 只调 `watchdog_register("/dev/watchdog0", ...)` 注册设备，**不 open、不 start**。NuttX `CONFIG_WATCHDOG_AUTOMONITOR` 是**被动**机制——只有用户态 `open("/dev/watchdog0")` 后，upper-half 才挂上工作队列周期喂狗。bringup 没有任何进程 open 它，所以 APB WDT 也无人喂 → ~8s 复位。

注释里写「start() does that when the upper-half opens the device」——但 bringup 里没 open，等于不喂。

## 修复方案

两条路任选其一（推荐**方案 A**，最小改动且行为确定）：

### 方案 A：app 主动接管两条狗（推荐）

bringup 进 app **第一时间**就处理 bootloader 留下的两条狗：

1. `bk7258_wdt_initialize()` 内，注册完 `/dev/watchdog0` 后，**主动 `start()` APB WDT**（直接调 lower-half `start`），让 NuttX automonitor 接管喂狗。`CONFIG_WATCHDOG_AUTOMONITOR=y` 已经配好 ping interval=4s，但需要 start 才生效——automonitor 在 device 被 open 时启动，所以板级应主动 open + start。
2. **AON WDT 要么关掉，要么纳入喂狗**。最干净的做法：进 app 后**关闭 AON WDT**（key1+period=0, key2+period=0），只保留 APB WDT 由 NuttX 管。理由：NuttX 没有双 WDT upper-half 概念，AON WDT 留着就必须有人喂，不如关。若要保留 AON 作为 fallback，则在 APB 喂狗回调里同步喂 AON。

**具体改动**：

`bk7258_wdt.c` 加 AON WDT 支持 + 主动 start：
- 新增 `BK7258_AON_WDT_BASE 0x44000600u` / `BK7258_AON_WDT_CTRL`
- `bk7258_wdt_initialize()` 末尾增加：
  - 关 AON WDT（或加到 keepalive 里同步喂）
  - 主动 open + start APB WDT：用 `start()` 把 priv->started=true 并 armed，触发 automonitor

`bk7258_bringup.c` 不变（仍只调 `bk7258_wdt_initialize`），由 initialize 内部保证 start。

### 方案 B：bootloader 跳 app 前关 AON WDT

在 `boot_main.c` 跳转 app 前，`boot_wdt_init()` 把 AON WDT 关掉（只保留 APB）。app 侧只需修缺陷 2（主动 start APB）。缺点：bootloader 还是手写，且 cold 路径若需 AON 兜底就没了。

## 详细 Findings

### DR-001: AON WDT 缺失导致复位循环 [Critical]
- **维度**：L1-7 嵌入式专项（P-48 硬件寄存器 / W1C，P-49 ISR/外设生命周期）
- **文件**：`bk7258_wdt.c` 全文
- **现象**：`bk7258_wdt.c` 无任何 `0x44000600` 引用，AON WDT armed 后无人喂
- **修复**：见方案 A.2——initialize 时关 AON WDT：`putreg32(WDT_KEY1<<16, AON_CTRL); putreg32(WDT_KEY2<<16, AON_CTRL);`（period=0 关狗，复用 APB stop 序列）

### DR-002: APB WDT 未 start，automonitor 不生效 [Critical]
- **维度**：L1-3 资源管理（生命周期不对称）
- **文件**：`bk7258_wdt.c:280-299` `bk7258_wdt_initialize`
- **现象**：register 后不 open/start，`CONFIG_WATCHDOG_AUTOMONITOR` 被动机制不触发
- **修复**：initialize 末尾主动 start（调内部 `bk7258_wdt_start`），并确保有进程/板级 open `/dev/watchdog0` 启动 automonitor；或用 `CONFIG_WATCHDOG_REGISTER` + 板级主动 open

### DR-003: keepalive 清 status 方向可能错误 [High]
- **维度**：L1-7（P-48 W1C 寄存器）
- **文件**：`bk7258_wdt.c:206`
- **现象**：`putreg32(getreg32(STATUS) & ~0x3, STATUS)` 是**读-改-写清 bit**，但 BK WDT status 是 W1C——应直接写 `0 << bit`（写 0 清），而 `& ~0x3` 读改写会把其它位也写回。bootloader `boot_wdt.h:106` 也是同样的写法（已板端工作），所以此处大概率无害，但与 SDK `wdt_ll` 不完全一致
- **修复**：参考 bootloader 已验证写法保留即可，但建议确认 status 是否 W1C；若是 W1C，直接 `putreg32(0, STATUS)` 更安全

### DR-004: getstatus timeleft 永远返回 timeout（失真）[Medium]
- **维度**：L1-6 输入边界
- **文件**：`bk7258_wdt.c:228`
- **现象**：注释承认无可读计数器，timeleft 固定返回 timeout。automonitor 依赖 timeleft 判断剩余时间，恒等于 timeout 会让等待逻辑退化（实际未必致命，因为 automonitor 是定时喂不是按 timeleft 喂）
- **修复**：可接受现状，但 automonitor 若依赖 timeleft 需确认

### DR-005: SYS_CTRL 配置在 start 里改，未与 bootloader 对齐校验 [Medium]
- **维度**：L1-7
- **文件**：`bk7258_wdt.c:157-159`
- **现象**：start 里无条件 `(v & ~0x3F) | 0x26` 重写 SYS_CTRL。bootloader 已设过，重复写无害，但若 SDK app 用不同值会冲突。bootloader 用 `0x26`，注释自洽
- **修复**：保留，无需改

### DR-006: stop 写 period=0 顺序与 SDK close 一致性 [Low]
- **维度**：L1-7
- **文件**：`bk7258_wdt.c:183-184`
- **现象**：stop 用 key1+0 / key2+0，与 SDK `wdt_hal_close` 一致，无问题
- **修复**：无需改

## Preparation

### 1) Clarify scope and expectations

- Identify the NuttX driver subsystem (sensor, serial, timer, analog, etc.).
- Confirm target bus (I2C, SPI, 1-Wire, etc.) and required hardware properties.
- Clarify the NuttX source tree location. The driver code lives under `nuttx/drivers/`.

### 2) Find reference drivers

> [!NOTE] Two types of reference drivers serve different purposes
>
> - **骨架参考（NuttX API 模式）**: 优先使用 NuttX in-tree 同类驱动作为代码骨架，确保符合 NuttX 的 upper-half/lower-half 架构和 VFS 集成方式
> - **芯片参考（寄存器/时序验证）**: 优先使用 Linux/Zephyr 同芯片驱动，用于交叉验证 datasheet 的寄存器定义、初始化序列、SPI 帧格式等芯片专属知识
>
> When used standalone: 手动搜索两类参考驱动
> When used with `driver-workflow` agent: Step A.2 自动完成两条线的并行搜索

Always look at the in-tree NuttX drivers before doing any work. There might already be a driver that (best scenario at the top):

1. Is exactly the same part as the one you are working on
2. Targets a very similar part from the same vendor (e.g., BMP280 vs BME680)
3. Is the same device subsystem as yours (e.g., another I2C sensor)

If a reference driver is found, use it as a **skeleton template**:

1. Copy the source file structure (function signatures, bus access pattern, registration flow, file layout)
2. Replace all device-specific content: register definitions, chip ID values, vendor/chip names, init sequences, calibration logic
3. After generating code, grep for the original chip name — zero matches required
4. **Do NOT copy register addresses or chip-specific constants** — these must come from the target device's datasheet

Re-use these files/folders whenever possible:
- Header files in `include/nuttx/sensors/`, `include/nuttx/i2c/`, etc.
- Existing board-level registration patterns in `boards/`

If no suitable reference driver exists:

1. Use the dispatch table below to load the subsystem-specific pattern reference
2. Use the most similar subsystem's reference driver as template (e.g., use accelerometer driver as template for gyro)
3. Follow the architectural pattern (uORB vs chardev) strictly from the loaded reference
4. For 🔲 Planned subsystems, use `chardev_pattern.md` (Production-Quality Skeleton section) as the starting point

#### Pattern A: Upper-Half / Lower-Half — Preferred for Subsystem Drivers

Most NuttX driver subsystems (sensors, timers, serial, audio, etc.) use an upper-half/lower-half split. The upper-half provides the VFS interface and common logic; you only implement the lower-half callbacks.

```
Application
    │  open/read/write/ioctl/poll
    ▼
  VFS (/dev/...)
    │
    ▼
  Upper-half (provided by NuttX)  ← Generic, handles VFS + common logic
    │  subsystem-specific callbacks
    ▼
  Lower-half (your driver)  ← You implement these
    │
    ▼
  Bus API (I2C_TRANSFER / SPI_*)
```

**When to use**: Always prefer this when the subsystem provides an upper-half framework. Load the corresponding reference document from the dispatch table for implementation details.

#### Pattern B: Standalone Character Device Driver

The simplest pattern. The driver directly implements `struct file_operations` and registers with `register_driver()`.

```
Application
    │  open/read/write/ioctl/close
    ▼
  VFS (/dev/mydevN)
    │
    ▼
  file_operations  ← Your driver implements these
    │
    ▼
  Bus API (I2C_TRANSFER / SPI_LOCK+SPI_SELECT+SPI_RECVBLOCK)
```

**When to use**: Only when the device doesn't fit any existing subsystem, or when existing in-tree drivers for the same device class already use this pattern (e.g., some vibrator or custom peripheral drivers).

See `references/chardev_pattern.md` for standalone character device implementation details.

The following sections cover **cross-subsystem generic patterns** that apply to all driver types.

#### Bus Access (I2C / SPI)

For I2C/SPI register read/write helpers, bulk transfer patterns, SPI frame protocols (8-bit and 16-bit), and SPI mode detection — read `references/bus_access.md` when writing bus access code.

### Write the Public Header File

if <SUBSYSTEM>_MYDEVICE

choice
	prompt "MYDEVICE Interface"
	default <SUBSYSTEM>_MYDEVICE_SPI

config <SUBSYSTEM>_MYDEVICE_I2C
	bool "MYDEVICE I2C Interface"
	select I2C
	---help---
		Enables support for the I2C interface

config <SUBSYSTEM>_MYDEVICE_SPI
	bool "MYDEVICE SPI Interface"
	select SPI
	---help---
		Enables support for the SPI interface

endchoice

endif # <SUBSYSTEM>_MYDEVICE
```

Key Kconfig conventions:
- Use `select I2C` or `select SPI` to auto-enable bus dependency
- Use `depends on` for soft dependencies
- Group device-specific options inside `if ... endif`
- Provide `---help---` text for every user-visible option
- For devices supporting both I2C and SPI, use a `choice` block
- Default interface should match the most common usage (check reference designs)

### Make.defs

Add your source file to `drivers/<subsystem>/Make.defs`:

```makefile
ifeq ($(CONFIG_<SUBSYSTEM>_MYDEVICE),y)
  CSRCS += mydevice.c
endif
```

> [!NOTE] File naming convention
>
> - Upper-half/lower-half drivers with framework: `mydevice_uorb.c` (sensors), `mydevice.c` (others)
> - Standalone char device drivers: `mydevice.c`
> - Check existing in-tree drivers for the naming convention used in your subsystem.
> - The Make.defs entry does NOT need to be under an `ifeq ($(CONFIG_I2C),y)` guard
>   if the Kconfig already uses `select I2C` — the bus will always be enabled.

The Make.defs file **must** end with the DEPPATH/VPATH/CFLAGS block (already present in existing files).

### CMakeLists.txt

Add your source file to `drivers/<subsystem>/CMakeLists.txt`:

```cmake
if(CONFIG_<SUBSYSTEM>_MYDEVICE)
  list(APPEND SRCS mydevice.c)
endif()
```

### Board-Level Registration

See `references/board_registration.md` for complete board-level registration patterns for both upper-half/lower-half and standalone char device drivers.

## NuttX Coding & Kernel API Rules

For all coding style rules, kernel API usage, initialization timing, work queue selection, interrupt patterns, synchronization primitives, RPMsg rules, and error cleanup patterns — read `references/coding_rules.md` when writing or reviewing driver code.

Quick reference (always run after generating code):

```bash
nuttx/tools/checkpatch.sh -f <your_file.c>
```

## Code Review

6-dimension review covering initialization, power management, API usage,
critical section & ISR, runtime environment, and coding style.

### Review Process

1. Read `.c`, `.h`, Kconfig, Make.defs, CMakeLists.txt. Identify driver pattern
   (uORB sensor / standalone chardev / RPMsg / other upper-half/lower-half).
2. Run 6-dimension checklist — mark each item PASS / WARN / FAIL.
   See [driver_review_checklist.md](references/driver_review_checklist.md).
3. Run nxstyle check: `nuttx/tools/checkpatch.sh -f <file.c>` (skip if unavailable).
4. Generate structured report (template in checklist reference).
5. For each FAIL/WARN: provide line number + fix snippet + rule reference.

### Review Rules

- FAIL items must be fixed before submission. Auto-fix and re-check until zero FAIL.
- WARN items are listed for user decision.
- If more than 5 issues found on file save, recommend running full review.

1	# NuttX Watchdog Driver Pattern
2	
3	## 框架概述
4	
5	NuttX watchdog 子系统采用标准的 upper-half/lower-half 分层架构：
6	
7	- **Upper-half**（`nuttx/drivers/timers/watchdog.c`）：提供字符设备接口（open/close/ioctl），处理 IOCTL 命令分发，管理 automonitor 功能
8	- **Lower-half**（芯片/板级实现）：实现硬件相关的 watchdog 操作（start/stop/keepalive/settimeout 等）
9	
10	```
11	应用层
12	  │  open("/dev/watchdog0") → ioctl(WDIOC_START/STOP/KEEPALIVE/...)
13	  ▼
14	Upper-half (nuttx/drivers/timers/watchdog.c)
15	  │  ops->start / ops->stop / ops->keepalive / ...
16	  ▼
17	Lower-half (芯片驱动实现 struct watchdog_ops_s)
18	  │  硬件寄存器操作
19	  ▼
20	Watchdog 硬件
21	```
22	
23	## 关键头文件
24	
25	```
26	nuttx/include/nuttx/timers/watchdog.h
27	```
28	
29	## Lower-half Ops 结构体定义
30	
31	```c
32	struct watchdog_ops_s
33	{
34	  /* Required methods */
35	
36	  CODE int (*start)(FAR struct watchdog_lowerhalf_s *lower);
37	  CODE int (*stop)(FAR struct watchdog_lowerhalf_s *lower);
38	
39	  /* Optional methods */
40	
41	  CODE int (*keepalive)(FAR struct watchdog_lowerhalf_s *lower);
42	  CODE int (*getstatus)(FAR struct watchdog_lowerhalf_s *lower,
43	                        FAR struct watchdog_status_s *status);
44	  CODE int (*settimeout)(FAR struct watchdog_lowerhalf_s *lower,
45	                         uint32_t timeout);
46	  CODE xcpt_t (*capture)(FAR struct watchdog_lowerhalf_s *lower,
47	                         CODE xcpt_t handler);
48	  CODE int (*ioctl)(FAR struct watchdog_lowerhalf_s *lower, int cmd,
49	                    unsigned long arg);
50	};
51	```
52	
53	### Ops 回调说明
54	
55	| Ops | 必选/可选 | 说明 |
56	|-----|----------|------|
57	| `start` | **必选** | 启动 watchdog 定时器，开始倒计时 |
58	| `stop` | **必选** | 停止 watchdog 定时器 |
59	| `keepalive` | 可选 | 喂狗（ping/pet），重置倒计时到当前 timeout 值 |
60	| `getstatus` | 可选 | 获取当前状态（flags + timeout + timeleft） |
61	| `settimeout` | 可选 | 设置新的超时值（毫秒），并重置定时器 |
62	| `capture` | 可选 | 设置超时回调（替代复位行为），返回旧 handler |
63	| `ioctl` | 可选 | 处理 upper-half 未识别的自定义 IOCTL |
64	
65	## Lower-half 状态结构体
66	
67	```c
68	struct watchdog_lowerhalf_s
69	{
70	  FAR const struct watchdog_ops_s *ops;  /* Lower half operations */
71	  /* 驱动私有数据跟在后面（cast-compatible） */
72	};
73	```
74	
75	典型的驱动私有结构体扩展模式：
76	
77	```c
78	struct my_wdg_lowerhalf_s
79	{
80	  const struct watchdog_ops_s *ops;  /* 必须是第一个字段 */
81	  uint32_t timeout;                  /* 当前超时值（ms） */
82	  bool started;                      /* 是否已启动 */
83	  xcpt_t handler;                    /* 用户超时回调 */
84	  void *upper;                       /* upper-half handle（用于 unregister） */
85	  /* ... 其他硬件相关字段 ... */
86	};
87	```
88	
89	## 设备注册 API
90	
91	```c
92	/* 标准注册（无 automonitor） */
93	FAR void *watchdog_register(FAR const char *path,
94	                            FAR struct watchdog_lowerhalf_s *lower);
95	
96	/* 带 oneshot automonitor */
97	FAR void *watchdog_register(FAR const char *path,
98	                            FAR struct watchdog_lowerhalf_s *lower,
99	                            FAR struct oneshot_lowerhalf_s *oneshot);
100	
101	/* 带 timer automonitor */
102	FAR void *watchdog_register(FAR const char *path,
103	                            FAR struct watchdog_lowerhalf_s *lower,
104	                            FAR struct timer_lowerhalf_s *timer);
105	```
106	
107	- **返回值**：成功返回非 NULL handle（用于 `watchdog_unregister`），失败返回 NULL
108	- **调用时机**：在 `up_lateinitialize()` 或 `board_late_initialize()` 中调用
109	- **设备路径约定**：`/dev/watchdog0`、`/dev/watchdog1`... 或自定义路径如 `/dev/wdt_cpu0`
110	
111	```c
112	void watchdog_unregister(FAR void *handle);
113	```
114	
115	## IOCTL 命令表
116	
117	| IOCTL | 值 | 参数 | 说明 |
118	|-------|-----|------|------|
119	| `WDIOC_START` | `_WDIOC(0x001)` | 无 | 启动 watchdog |
120	| `WDIOC_STOP` | `_WDIOC(0x002)` | 无 | 停止 watchdog |
121	| `WDIOC_GETSTATUS` | `_WDIOC(0x003)` | `struct watchdog_status_s *` | 获取状态 |
122	| `WDIOC_SETTIMEOUT` | `_WDIOC(0x004)` | `uint32_t`（毫秒） | 设置超时 |
123	| `WDIOC_CAPTURE` | `_WDIOC(0x005)` | `struct watchdog_capture_s *` | 设置超时回调 |
124	| `WDIOC_KEEPALIVE` | `_WDIOC(0x006)` | 无 | 喂狗 |
125	| `WDIOC_SETSOFT` | `_WDIOC(0x007)` | 无 | 设置为软件 watchdog |
126	| `WDIOC_SETWINDOW` | `_WDIOC(0x008)` | `struct watchdog_window_s *` | 设置窗口值 |
127	| `WDIOC_MINTIME` | `_WDIOC(0x080)` | `uint32_t`（毫秒） | 设置最小 ping 间隔 |
128	
129	## 状态结构体
130	
131	```c
132	struct watchdog_status_s
133	{
134	  uint32_t flags;     /* WDFLAGS_ACTIVE | WDFLAGS_RESET | WDFLAGS_CAPTURE */
135	  uint32_t timeout;   /* 当前超时设置（毫秒） */
136	  uint32_t timeleft;  /* 距离超时的剩余时间（毫秒） */
137	};
138	
139	struct watchdog_capture_s
140	{
141	  CODE xcpt_t newhandler;  /* 新的超时回调 */
142	  CODE xcpt_t oldhandler;  /* 返回旧的超时回调 */
143	};
144	
145	struct watchdog_window_s
146	{
147	  uint32_t lwindow;  /* 左窗口值（毫秒） */
148	  uint32_t rwindow;  /* 右窗口值（毫秒） */
149	};
150	```
151	
152	## 状态标志位
153	
154	| 标志 | 值 | 说明 |
155	|------|-----|------|
156	| `WDFLAGS_ACTIVE` | `(1 << 0)` | watchdog 正在运行 |
157	| `WDFLAGS_RESET` | `(1 << 1)` | 超时时执行系统复位 |
158	| `WDFLAGS_CAPTURE` | `(1 << 2)` | 超时时调用用户回调 |
159	
160	## Automonitor 机制
161	
162	NuttX watchdog 框架支持 automonitor 功能——由内核自动喂狗，无需应用层参与。通过 Kconfig 配置：
163	
164	- `CONFIG_WATCHDOG_AUTOMONITOR_BY_ONESHOT` — 使用 oneshot timer 自动喂狗
165	- `CONFIG_WATCHDOG_AUTOMONITOR_BY_TIMER` — 使用 timer 自动喂狗
166	- `CONFIG_WATCHDOG_AUTOMONITOR_BY_WQUEUE` — 使用 work queue 自动喂狗
167	- `CONFIG_WATCHDOG_AUTOMONITOR_BY_CAPTURE` — 使用 capture 回调自动喂狗
168	- `CONFIG_WATCHDOG_AUTOMONITOR_BY_IDLE` — 在 idle 线程中自动喂狗
169	
170	automonitor 在 `watchdog_register()` 时自动启动（如果配置了），lower-half 驱动无需额外处理。
171	
172	## MCAL API → NuttX Ops 映射表
173	
174	| NuttX Ops | MCAL API（AUTOSAR 标准名） | 说明 |
175	|-----------|---------------------------|------|
176	| `start` | `Wdg_SetMode(WDGIF_SLOW_MODE)` + `Wdg_SetTriggerCondition(timeout)` | MCAL WDG Init 后默认处于 DefaultMode，start 确保进入活跃模式并设置初始 trigger |
177	| `stop` | `Wdg_SetMode(WDGIF_OFF_MODE)` | 关闭 watchdog（需 `DisableAllowed=TRUE`） |
178	| `keepalive` | `Wdg_SetTriggerCondition(current_timeout)` | 重新触发 watchdog 计时 |
179	| `getstatus` | 无直接对应 | 从适配层内部状态返回 |
180	| `settimeout` | `Wdg_SetTriggerCondition(new_timeout)` | 设置新超时并触发 |
181	| `capture` | 无直接对应 | MCAL WDG 无用户回调机制，仅适配层内部记录 handler |
182	| `ioctl` | — | 可扩展支持 `WDIOC_SETWINDOW` 映射到 MCAL 窗口百分比 |
183	
184	### MCAL WDG 模式说明
185	
186	AUTOSAR WDG 定义三种模式（`WdgIf_ModeType`）：
187	
188	| 模式 | 含义 | 对应 NuttX 行为 |
189	|------|------|----------------|
190	| `WDGIF_OFF_MODE` | 关闭 watchdog | `stop` ops |
191	| `WDGIF_SLOW_MODE` | 慢速模式（长超时） | 默认运行模式 |
192	| `WDGIF_FAST_MODE` | 快速模式（短超时） | 可通过 ioctl 切换 |
193	
194	### MCAL WDG 关键行为
195	
196	1. **`Wdg_Init(ConfigPtr)`** — 初始化 WDG 模块，进入 `DefaultMode`（通常是 SLOW_MODE）。Init 后 WDG **立即开始计时**。
197	2. **`Wdg_SetTriggerCondition(timeout)`** — 设置下一个超时周期（毫秒）。必须在窗口期内调用，否则被拒绝。
198	3. **`Wdg_SetMode(mode)`** — 切换模式。切换到 OFF_MODE 需要 `DisableAllowed=TRUE`。
199	4. **窗口机制** — WDG 有窗口百分比配置（`WindowSizePercentage[3]`），在窗口外调用 SetTriggerCondition 会报错。
200	
201	### 适配层设计要点
202	
203	1. **Init 后自动启动问题**：MCAL `Wdg_Init()` 后 WDG 立即开始计时，但 NuttX 框架期望 `start` ops 才启动。适配层需要在 Init 后立即开始内部喂狗（或依赖 automonitor），直到用户显式 start。
204	2. **stop 可能被拒绝**：如果 EB 配置 `DisableAllowed=FALSE`，`Wdg_SetMode(WDGIF_OFF_MODE)` 会返回 `E_NOT_OK`。适配层 `stop` ops 应返回 `-EPERM`。
205	3. **timeout 截断**：MCAL 有 `FastModeMaxTimeout` 和 `SlowModeMaxTimeout` 限制。如果用户请求的 timeout 超过当前模式最大值，适配层应截断到最大值并返回成功（或返回 `-EINVAL`）。
206	4. **无中断**：MCAL WDG 模块没有 ISR，不需要中断路由。超时直接触发硬件复位（或 NMI trap）。
207	
208	## 参考实现
209	
210	- **iLLD 参考**：`vendor/infineon/chips/aurix/aurix_wdg.c` — 使用 iLLD API 实现的 NuttX watchdog lower-half
211	- **NuttX in-tree 参考**：`nuttx/drivers/timers/watchdog.c` — upper-half 实现
212	- **MCAL 适配骨架**：`frameworks/system/autocore/mcal/uart.c` — MCAL UART 适配层（结构参考）

## Files reviewed

- `/home/lijian/project/open-vela/contest2026_135_yongwangzhiqian/board/bk7258_t5ai/chip/bk7258_wdt.c`

- `/home/lijian/project/open-vela/contest2026_135_yongwangzhiqian/board/bk7258_t5ai/bootloader/boot_wdt.h`
- SDK references: `wdt_driver.c`, `wdt_hal.c`, `wdt_ll.h` (bk7258), `wdt_struct.h`, `aon_wdt_driver.c`, `aon_wdt_ll.h`, `aon_wdt_hal.c`, `wdt_reg.h`, `watchdog.c` (NuttX upper-half)

### WDT-01: AON WDT armed by bootloader, never fed after handoff -- reboot-loop root cause

**Severity: CRITICAL**
**Files:** `boot_wdt.h:89-94`, `bk7258_wdt.c` (entire file), `bk7258_bringup.c:172`

**Deep-logic trace:**

The bootloader's `boot_wdt_init()` arms **both** watchdogs:
1. APB WDT @ `0x44800000` -- key1+8000, key2+8000 (16-bit period field, full8000 stored, ~8s at ~1kHz)
2. AON WDT @ `0x44000600` -- same key sequence with same8000 value

However, the AON WDT's `ctrl` register has an **8-bit period field** (bits[23:16] per `aon_wdt_ll.h:31`: `AON_WDT_CONFIG_WD_PERIOD_MASK = 0xff`), **not** 16-bit like APB WDT. The bootloader writes8000 (0x1F50); after the8-bit mask the AON hardware stores only `0x50` = **80 ticks**. On the AON WDT's ~32kHz ROSC clock (with typical divider), 80 ticks is roughly **2.5ms**, not 8 seconds.

The bootloader's `boot_wdt_feed()` only feeds the APB WDT (clears `WDT_APB_STATUS`, re-arms `WDT_APB_CTRL`). It **never touches the AON WDT** after initial arming.

The NuttX driver (`bk7258_wdt.c`) only manages the APB WDT. It has **zero awareness of the AON WDT** -- no register writes to `0x44000600`, no calls to `bk_aon_wdt_feed()` or `bk_aon_wdt_stop()`.

**Resulting state machine:**
```
bootloader: boot_wdt_init() arms APB (8s) + AON (2.5ms)
bootloader: boot_wdt_feed() feeds APB only
bootloader: jumps to app
...2.5ms elapses, AON WDT fires, resets chip...
(reboot loop -- NuttX never gets past board_app_initialize)
```

Even if the AON clock is slower (e.g., making 80 ticks ~80ms), `board_app_initialize()` mounts procfs, registers DVFS procfs entries, and does flash MTD init **before** reaching `bk7258_wdt_initialize()` at line 172. Any of these can easily exceed 80ms, causing the AON WDT to reset the chip before the APB WDT is ever re-initialized.

**Fix direction:** In `bk7258_wdt_initialize()` or `board_app_initialize()`, **immediately stop or feed the AON WDT** before any other init:
```c
// Stop AON WDT (key sequence with period=0)
putreg32(0x5A0000u, 0x44000600u);
putreg32(0xA50000u, 0x44000600u);
```
Or call the SDK `bk_aon_wdt_stop()`. This must happen as the **very first thing** in `board_app_initialize()`, before procfs mount or any other potentially slow operation.

---

### WDT-02: keepalive() writes to wrong register (dev_version, not dev_status)

**Severity: HIGH**
**File:** `bk7258_wdt.c:206`

**Deep-logic trace:**

The driver defines:
```c
#define BK7258_WDT_STATUS  (BK7258_WDT_BASE + 0x04u)  // = 0x44800004
```

From `wdt_struct.h` (BK7258), the register layout by word offset is:
| Word idx | Byte offset | Field |
|----------|------------|-------|
| 0 | 0x00 | dev_id |
| 1 | 0x04 | **dev_version** |
| 2 | 0x08 | global_ctrl |
| 3 | 0x0C | dev_status |
| 4 | 0x10 | ctrl |

`0x44800004` maps to `dev_version`, **not** `dev_status` (which is at `0x4480000C`). The keepalive function:
```c
putreg32(getreg32(BK7258_WDT_STATUS) & ~0x3u, BK7258_WDT_STATUS);
```
This reads `dev_version`, clears its bits[1:0], and writes it back. The actual WDT status register at `0x0C` is **never cleared**.

The SDK's `wdt_hal_close()` never accesses offset 0x04; it writes to `global_ctrl` (0x08) and `ctrl` (0x10). The SDK's `wdt_ll_set_period()` resets the counter via `global_ctrl.soft_reset = 1` rather than clearing any status register, so the SDK does not depend on a status-clear step at all.

**Impact:** The keepalive path does not clear the actual watchdog status bits. If the hardware uses these status bits to determine whether the watchdog has expired (rather than just the counter), the watchdog may still fire despite the keepalive. In practice, the key-sequence re-arm in `bk7258_wdt_write_period()` is the primary feed mechanism, but the status clearing is a no-op against the intended target.

**Fix direction:** Change to `BK7258_WDT_BASE + 0x0C` if status clearing is actually needed, or remove the status-clear step entirely (the SDK's `bk_wdt_feed()` path via `wdt_ll_set_period()` does not clear status -- it relies on the soft reset to reset the counter).

---

### WDT-03: keepalive() omits soft_reset -- counter may not actually reset

**Severity: HIGH**
**File:** `bk7258_wdt.c:194-208`

**Deep-logic trace:**

The SDK's `bk_wdt_feed()` calls `wdt_hal_init_wdt()` which calls `wdt_ll_set_period()`, which **always** performs:
```c
hw->global_ctrl.soft_reset = 1;   // wdt_ll.h:80 -- resets WDT state machine
// then key1+period, key2+period
```

The NuttX driver's keepalive deliberately skips the soft reset:
```c
/* Do NOT soft_reset here -- soft_reset may clear the WDT clock gate */
putreg32(getreg32(BK7258_WDT_STATUS) & ~0x3u, BK7258_WDT_STATUS);
bk7258_wdt_write_period(priv->timeout);
```

The driver's comment says "soft_reset may clear the WDT clock gate" and notes "the SDK's wdt_init_common() re-powers the clock after soft_reset, but we don't have that call in keepalive."

However, examining the SDK flow: `bk_wdt_start()` calls `wdt_init_common()` (powers up clock) then `wdt_ll_set_period()` (soft_reset + key sequence). Subsequent `bk_wdt_feed()` calls `wdt_ll_set_period()` **without** calling `wdt_init_common()` first. This means the SDK itself does soft_reset on every feed without re-powering the clock. The SDK author evidently concluded that soft_reset does **not** gate the clock (or that the clock remains powered from the initial `wdt_init_common()` call).

The driver's fear of soft_reset gating the clock appears unfounded -- the SDK contradicts it. Without soft_reset, the WDT's internal state machine is not reset, and combined with WDT-02 (status write to wrong register), the keepalive effectively does nothing more than re-writing the period via the key sequence. Whether this actually resets the hardware counter depends on the BK7258 WDT implementation: if writing a new period via the key sequence resets the counter, this works; if not, the counter keeps counting and the watchdog can fire despite keepalive being called.

**Fix direction:** Add the soft_reset step to keepalive, matching the SDK:
```c
putreg32(1u, BK7258_WDT_GLOBAL_CTRL);  // soft_reset
bk7258_wdt_write_period(priv->timeout);
```
Remove the status-clear step (WDT-02 shows it targets the wrong register, and the SDK does not clear status on feed).

---

### WDT-04: settimeout() re-arms without soft_reset -- stale counter

**Severity: MEDIUM**
**File:** `bk7258_wdt.c:232-253`

**Deep-logic trace:**

When the WDT is already running and `settimeout()` is called:
```c
if (priv->started)
{
    bk7258_wdt_write_period(priv->timeout);  // key1+new_period, key2+new_period
}
```

This writes a new period via the key sequence but does **not** soft_reset the counter. If the counter is currently at value N and the new period is P where N < P, the effective timeout is (P - N), not P. For example, if the counter is at 7000 and the new period is 8000, the watchdog fires in 1000 ticks (~1s), not 8000 ticks (~8s).

The SDK's `bk_wdt_start()` (which is the equivalent operation) always calls `wdt_init_common()` + `wdt_ll_set_period()` which includes the soft_reset, ensuring the counter starts from 0 with the new period.

The NuttX automonitor calls `WD_SETTIMEOUT` followed by `WD_START` during initialization (lines 297-298 of `watchdog.c`). Since `start()` does a soft_reset, the automonitor initialization path is correct. The risk is only when `settimeout()` is called on an already-running watchdog via `WDIOC_SETTIMEOUT` ioctl.

**Fix direction:** Add soft_reset before re-arming:
```c
if (priv->started)
{
    putreg32(1u, BK7258_WDT_GLOBAL_CTRL);
    bk7258_wdt_write_period(priv->timeout);
}
```

---

### WDT-05: stop() uses soft_reset + key(0) -- correct but differs from bootloader

**Severity: LOW (informational)**
**File:** `bk7258_wdt.c:174-189`

**Deep-logic trace:**

The NuttX driver's `stop()`:
```c
putreg32(1u, BK7258_WDT_GLOBAL_CTRL);  // soft_reset
putreg32(BK7258_WDT_KEY1 << 16, BK7258_WDT_CTRL);  // key1 + period=0
putreg32(BK7258_WDT_KEY2 << 16, BK7258_WDT_CTRL);  // key2 + period=0
```

This matches the SDK's `wdt_hal_close()` (lines 58-67 of `wdt_hal.c`):
```c
REG_SET(SOC_WDT_REG_BASE + 4 * 2, 1, 1, 1);  // global_ctrl.soft_reset = 1
REG_WRITE(SOC_WDT_REG_BASE + 4 * 4, 0x5A0000);  // key1 + period=0
REG_WRITE(SOC_WDT_REG_BASE + 4 * 4, 0xA50000);  // key2 + period=0
```

The stop is correct and follows the SDK pattern. However, the bootloader's `boot_wdt_feed()` comment at `boot_wdt.h:100` says "clear APB_WDT status + reinit" which is a different pattern. The NuttX stop is consistent with the SDK, which is the right reference.

**No fix needed** for the APB WDT stop. But `stop()` does **not** stop the AON WDT (see WDT-01).

---

### WDT-06: SYS_CTRL read-modify-write in start() -- safe but fragile

**Severity: LOW**
**File:** `bk7258_wdt.c:157-159`

**Deep-logic trace:**
```c
uint32_t v = getreg32(BK7258_SYS_CTRL_REG);
v = (v & ~BK7258_WDT_SYSCTRL_MASK) | BK7258_WDT_SYSCTRL_VAL;
putreg32(v, BK7258_SYS_CTRL_REG);
```

This is a non-atomic read-modify-write. On a single-core Cortex-M (BK7258), this is safe as long as no interrupt handler modifies `SYS_CTRL` concurrently. The mask `0x3F` preserves bits[31:6], so other `SYS_CTRL` configuration is not clobbered. The operation is idempotent (writing the same value twice is harmless).

The risk is if another driver or interrupt handler does its own read-modify-write on `SYS_CTRL` between the `getreg32` and `putreg32`. In practice, during `start()` which runs in thread context, this is unlikely but not impossible. The SDK uses `sys_drv_dev_clk_pwr_up()` which presumably handles this atomically.

**Fix direction:** Consider wrapping in `irqsave()`/`irqrestore()` if `SYS_CTRL` is shared with interrupt-context writers, or use the SDK's `sys_drv_dev_clk_pwr_up()`.

---

### WDT-07: getstatus() timeleft always returns timeout

**Severity: LOW**
**File:** `bk7258_wdt.c:228`

The BK7258 APB WDT has no readable counter register. The driver returns `priv->timeout` as `timeleft`, which is an upper bound (the actual time left is between 0 and timeout). No NuttX upper-half code depends on accurate `timeleft` -- the automonitor uses only `keepalive` and `start/stop/settimeout`. External callers using `WDIOC_GETSTATUS` would get a stale value, but this is a hardware limitation.

**No fix needed.** A comment noting this is a hardware limitation (already present at line 225) is sufficient.

---

### WDT-08: DP-07 -- hand-written registers vs SDK APIs

**Severity: MEDIUM (design)**
**File:** `bk7258_wdt.c` (entire)

**Assessment of what the driver skips by not using the SDK:**

| SDK step | Driver equivalent | Status |
|----------|------------------|--------|
| `sys_drv_dev_clk_pwr_up(CLK_PWR_ID_WDG_CPU)` | SYS_CTRL RMW (partial) | Done, but non-atomically |
| `sys_hal_nmi_wdt_set_clk_div(3)` | Not done | **Missing** -- NMI WDT clock divider not configured |
| `aon_pmu_drv_wdt_rst_dev_enable()` | Not done | **Missing** -- relies on bootloader having done this |
| `wdt_hal_init()` (select WDT unit, close unused) | Not done | **Missing** -- neither APB nor AON "unused" WDT is closed |
| `bk_timer_start(TIMER_ID2, ...)` for periodic feed | Not needed (NuttX automonitor) | OK |
| `bk_aon_wdt_stop()` / `bk_aon_wdt_feed()` | Not done | **Missing** -- AON WDT orphaned (WDT-01) |
| `wdt_init_common()` before each soft_reset | Not done in keepalive | **Missing** -- may cause WDT-03 |

Hand-writing registers is justifiable for a NuttX lower-half driver that cannot depend on the full Beken SDK runtime (RTOS integration, `os_memset`, `GLOBAL_INT_*` macros, etc.). However, the driver should still replicate the **critical hardware init steps** that the SDK performs. The missing AON WDT handling (WDT-01) and missing clock/power init are the most significant gaps.

**Fix direction:** At minimum, add AON WDT stop/feed in `bk7258_wdt_initialize()`. Consider adding NMI WDT clock divider configuration and PMU WDT reset enable if the bootloader cannot be relied upon to have done these.

### F-01 -- AON WDT Never Fed in App Phase (Reboot Loop Root Cause)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| **ID** | F-01 |
| **Severity** | **Critical** |
| **Dimension** | L1-3 Resource Management, L1-7 Embedded |
| **Pattern** | Unhandled hardware watchdog causing reboot loop |
| **Location** | `bk7258_wdt.c` (entire file), `boot_wdt.h:92-94`, `start.S:70-75`, `boot_main.c:193` |
| **Confidence** | HIGH |

**Description:** The bootloader flow is:

1. `start.S:70-84` -- disarms both APB WDT and AON WDT (period=0).
2. `boot_main.c:193` -- `boot_wdt_init()` RE-ARMS both WDTs with `WDT_PERIOD=8000` (~8 seconds). This is the time origin T.
3. `boot_main.c:259` -- `boot_wdt_feed()` (feeds APB WDT only) then jumps to app.
4. App's `board_app_initialize()` calls `bk7258_wdt_initialize()` which registers only the APB WDT as `/dev/watchdog0`.
5. NuttX automonitor (`CONFIG_WATCHDOG_AUTOMONITOR=y`, `PING_INTERVAL=4`) feeds the APB WDT every 4 seconds.

The AON WDT at `0x44000600` is armed at time T by `boot_wdt_init()` and is NEVER fed again. After T+8s, the AON WDT expires and triggers a chip reset. This creates an infinite reboot loop: bootloader arms both WDTs, app only feeds APB WDT, AON WDT fires ~8s later, reset, repeat.

The SDK provides `bk_aon_wdt_feed()` and `bk_aon_wdt_stop()` APIs in `driver/aon_wdt.h` that are available but unused.

**Fix:** Either (a) stop the AON WDT early in app init via `bk_aon_wdt_stop()` before it expires, or (b) register a second watchdog lower-half instance for the AON WDT and feed it through the NuttX automonitor framework, or (c) have the APB WDT driver's `start()` or `keepalive()` also call `bk_aon_wdt_feed()` as a side-effect.

- `bk_wdt_feed()` -- feeds the WDT
- `bk_aon_wdt_feed()`, `bk_aon_wdt_stop()`, `bk_aon_wdt_set_period()` -- for AON WDT

The driver's own comments (lines 8-23) explicitly document the SDK-to-driver mapping, proving the author was aware of these APIs but chose to duplicate the logic. This creates a maintenance burden: if Beken updates the SDK register layout or adds errata workarounds, the hand-written driver will diverge.

The SDK's `wdt_ll_set_period()` (in `wdt_ll.h:50-87`) additionally handles `CONFIG_NMI_WDT_EN` clock divider scaling that the driver ignores entirely.

**Fix:** Replace raw register access with SDK API calls. The NuttX lower-half ops would become thin wrappers: `start()` -> `bk_wdt_start(priv->timeout)`, `stop()` -> `bk_wdt_stop()`, `keepalive()` -> `bk_wdt_feed()`, `settimeout()` -> `bk_wdt_start(new_timeout)`.

### F-03 -- watchdog_register() Return Value Ignored

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| **ID** | F-03 |
| **Severity** | **Medium** |
| **Dimension** | L1-4 Error Handling, L1-3 Resource Management |
| **Pattern** | Unchecked return value |
| **Location** | `bk7258_wdt.c:293-294` |
| **Confidence** | HIGH |

**Description:** At line 293, `watchdog_register()` returns a `void*` handle (non-NULL on success, NULL on failure per the pattern spec at wdg_pattern.md line 107). The return value is silently discarded. The function then returns `OK` unconditionally at line 298. If registration fails, the caller (`board_app_initialize`) has no indication, and the system proceeds without a watchdog -- the APB WDT continues running from the bootloader's armed state but no automonitor feeds it, leading to a reset within 8 seconds.

In `bk7258_bringup.c:172`, the return of `bk7258_wdt_initialize()` is also cast to `(void)`, compounding the issue.

**Fix:** Store the `watchdog_register()` return value and return an error (e.g., `-ENOMEM`) if it is NULL. Optionally store the handle for future `watchdog_unregister()` cleanup.

### F-04 -- No Concurrency Protection on Shared State

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| **ID** | F-04 |
| **Severity** | **Medium** |
| **Dimension** | L1-2 Concurrency Safety |
| **Pattern** | Data race on shared mutable state |
| **Location** | `bk7258_wdt.c:92-97` (struct fields), `bk7258_wdt.c:148-209` (all ops) |
| **Confidence** | MEDIUM |

**Description:** The `bk7258_wdt_lowerhalf_s` structure has `timeout` (uint32_t) and `started` (bool) fields that are read and written by multiple ops without any lock. With `CONFIG_WATCHDOG_AUTOMONITOR=y`, the automonitor work queue calls `keepalive()` periodically from a different execution context than user-initiated `ioctl` calls to `settimeout()` or `stop()`. On ARM Cortex-M33 (BK7258), a 32-bit aligned write is atomic, but the sequence in `settimeout()` (lines 243-249) writes `timeout` then conditionally calls `bk7258_wdt_write_period()` -- between these two operations, `keepalive()` could read the new `timeout` but the WDT hardware still has the old period, or vice versa.

The risk is low in practice because the automonitor interval (4s) is much larger than the critical section, but it is a correctness issue.

**Fix:** Use `irqsave()`/`irqrestore()` around the critical sections in ops that modify or read shared state, or use a lightweight spinlock.

### F-05 -- W1C Register Read-Modify-Write in keepalive()

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| **ID** | F-05 |
| **Severity** | **Medium** |
| **Dimension** | L1-7 Embedded (W1C register handling) |
| **Pattern** | Unsafe read-modify-write on potentially W1C status register |
| **Location** | `bk7258_wdt.c:206` |
| **Confidence** | MEDIUM |

**Description:** Line 206 performs:
```c
putreg32(getreg32(BK7258_WDT_STATUS) & ~0x3u, BK7258_WDT_STATUS);
```

The STATUS register at `0x44800004` has bits[1:0] documented as status flags that are cleared by writing. If bits[1:0] are Write-1-to-Clear (W1C), the intent of `& ~0x3u` is to write 0 to those bits, which would NOT clear W1C bits (W1C requires writing 1 to clear). This means the status clear may be a no-op for W1C bits.

Conversely, if the register has OTHER W1C bits beyond [1:0], the read-modify-write would write back 1s to those bits (from the read), inadvertently clearing them.

The SDK's `wdt_hal_init_wdt()` (the SDK's feed path) does NOT touch the STATUS register at all -- it only re-writes the period via key sequence. The bootloader's `boot_wdt_feed()` does the same read-modify-write, so the driver is consistent with the bootloader, but both may be incorrect.

**Fix:** Determine the exact STATUS register bit semantics from the BK7258 TRM. If bits[1:0] are W1C, write `0x3u` to clear them (not read-modify-write). If they are regular R/W1S or plain W, the current approach is correct. Alternatively, follow the SDK pattern and skip the status clear entirely -- just reinit the period.

### F-06 -- settimeout(0) Accidentally Disables WDT

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| **ID** | F-06 |
| **Severity** | **Medium** |
| **Dimension** | L1-6 Input Boundary |
| **Pattern** | Zero-value input triggers unintended shutdown behavior |
| **Location** | `bk7258_wdt.c:232-254` |
| **Confidence** | HIGH |

**Description:** `bk7258_wdt_settimeout()` only caps at the maximum (line 238-241: `timeout > BK7258_WDT_PERIOD_MASK`) but does not reject a timeout of 0. Per the SDK's `close_wdt()` / `wdt_hal_close()` pattern (wdt_hal.c:61-66), writing key+period=0 is the "close WDT" command. If `settimeout(0)` is called while `started==true`, the driver writes period=0 to the WDT control register (via `bk7258_wdt_write_period(0)`), which arms the WDT with a zero-length period. On the BK7258, this either immediately fires the WDT or disables it (depending on hardware interpretation of period=0). Either outcome is unintended for a `settimeout` call.

**Fix:** Reject `timeout == 0` (and possibly very small values below a safe minimum) with `-EINVAL`.

### F-07 -- start() soft_reset Without Re-Powering Clock

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| **ID** | F-07 |
| **Severity** | **Medium** |
| **Dimension** | L1-7 Embedded (hardware sequencing) |
| **Pattern** | Incomplete hardware init sequence |
| **Location** | `bk7258_wdt.c:162-163` |
| **Confidence** | MEDIUM |

**Description:** `bk7258_wdt_start()` writes `1u` to `BK7258_WDT_GLOBAL_CTRL` (line 163) to soft-reset the WDT state machine. The driver's own comment at line 203-205 in `keepalive()` acknowledges: "soft_reset may clear the WDT clock gate (the SDK's wdt_init_common() re-powers the clock after soft_reset, but we don't have that call in keepalive)."

The SDK's `wdt_ll_set_period()` does the same soft_reset, but the SDK's `wdt_init_common()` (called from `bk_wdt_start()`) re-powers the WDT clock via `pm_clock_ctrl()` before calling `wdt_hal_init_wdt()`. The driver's `start()` does the soft_reset but does NOT re-enable the WDT clock. If the bootloader's SYS_CTRL config at line 157-159 is sufficient to keep the clock alive across soft_reset, this is fine. But if the soft_reset gates the clock, the WDT would silently stop counting.

**Fix:** Either (a) call the SDK's clock enable API before soft_reset, or (b) remove the soft_reset from `start()` and only do it if absolutely needed (with clock re-enable), or (c) use `bk_wdt_start()` which handles the full sequence.

### F-08 -- stop() Uses soft_reset + period=0 Pattern Without SDK Confirmation

| Field | Value |

| **ID** | F-08 |
| **Severity** | **Low** |
| **Dimension** | L1-7 Embedded |

| **Confidence** | MEDIUM |

**Description:** The `stop()` function does a soft_reset (line 182) then writes key+period=0 (lines 183-184). **Fix:** Follow the SDK's close sequence exactly, or use `bk_wdt_stop()`.

重要纠错。Round 2 的 WDT-01 **深度事实判断错了**。看 `aon_wdt_ll.h`：

- `AON_WDT_CONFIG_WD_PERIOD_POS = 16`，`AON_WDT_CONFIG_WD_PERIOD_MASK = 0xff` —— period 在 **bit[16..23]**（8 位），但 `AON_WDT_F_PERIOD_M` 在 reg.h 里是 `0xffff`（16 位）。LL 层用 `AON_WDT_F_PERIOD_M` (16 位) 写入 ctrl 的低 16 位，key 在 bit16+。

但同时 APB WDT（`boot_wdt.h`）和 AON WDT 的 LL 接口不同。bootloader 的 `boot_wdt_init` 对 AON WDT 写的是 `(KEY<<16)|(period&0xFFFF)`——period 放低 16 位、key 放 bit16+，这与 `aon_wdt_ll_set_period` 一致。所以 **Round 2 说的"AON WDT 是 8-bit period，8000 被截成 0x50=2.5ms"是误读**——`AON_WDT_CONFIG_WD_PERIOD_MASK 0xff` 是 LL 一个 get 函数用的窄掩码，实际 set 用的是 `AON_WDT_F_PERIOD_M=0xffff` 16 位。

**所以根因仍是"AON WDT armed 后无人喂，~8s 复位"**，不是 2.5ms。这点两轮一致。

# Stage B2-Fix — WDT 驱动修复：AON WDT 无人喂导致进 app 无限重启

> **范围**：BK7258 NuttX WDT 驱动审查（driver-code-reviewer 双轮）+ 修复进 app 后 ~8s 无限重启的根因。
> **状态**：审查完成（双轮交叉验证），修复方案已定，待实施板端验证。
> **根因**：bootloader `boot_wdt_init()` 同时 arm APB WDT（`0x44800000`）与 AON WDT（`0x44000600`），
> period=8000（~8s）。app 只接管 APB WDT（NuttX automonitor 在 `watchdog_register()` 时自动 `WD_START`+
> 每 4s `WD_KEEPALIVE`），**AON WDT 零处理** → ~8s 后 AON WDT 超时复位 → 无限重启。

---

## 1. 审查方法

按 `driver-code-reviewer` skill 双轮 subagent 独立审查：
- **Round 1**（59 Pattern + DP-07 重复造轮子，参照 `nuttx-driver-development/references/wdg_pattern.md`）
- **Round 2**（深层逻辑：生命周期对称性、boot handoff 状态机、并发竞态）

裁判交叉验证两轮结论。

### 1.1 已纠正的早期误判

| 早期判断 | 纠正后 | 依据 |
|---|---|---|
| "APB WDT 没人喂 → 重启"（DR-002） | **撤回**。APB WDT 由 NuttX automonitor 在 register 时自动接管 | `nuttx/drivers/timers/watchdog.c:786-798` + `watchdog_automonitor_start` 在 register 路径内调 `WD_START`+`WD_SETTIMEOUT`；defconfig `BY_WDOG` 默认 + `PING_INTERVAL=4` |
| "进 app 前手写寄存器关 AON" | 方案改为：AON WDT 关狗用与 bootloader 一致的 key 协议（已板端验证），不引入 SDK AON 子系统 | `boot_wdt.h` AON key 序列已验证；SDK `wdt_driver.c` 依赖全栈，AON WDT 改 SDK 收益不抵成本 |
| Round 2 称"AON WDT 8-bit period→8000 截成 2.5ms" | **误读**。`aon_wdt_ll_set_period` 用 `AON_WDT_F_PERIOD_M=0xffff`（16 位），`0xff` 掩码只是某 get 函数的窄掩码 | `aon_wdt_ll.h` set 用 16 位 period，key 在 bit16+，与 `boot_wdt.h` 一致 |

---

## 2. 双轮交叉验证结果

### 2.1 两轮一致确认（高置信度）

| Finding | R1 | R2 | 严重度 | 置信度 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **AON WDT 无人喂 → 重启循环** | F-01 | WDT-01 | **Critical** | HIGH |

两轮独立定位**同一根因**，完全一致。这是进 app 无限重启的**唯一根因**。

### 2.2 采纳的有效问题（两轮一致或高价值）

| Finding | 来源 | 严重度 | 处理 |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-07 重复造轮子（手写寄存器 vs SDK `bk_wdt_*`） | F-02/WDT-08 | High | APB WDT 不改 SDK（依赖全栈，板端已稳）；AON 关狗沿用 bootloader 已验证协议 |
| `watchdog_register()` 返回值未检查 | F-03 | Medium | 修复时加检查 |
| `settimeout(0)` 等于关狗 | F-06 | Medium | 加 `timeout==0` 拒绝 |
| `settimeout` 运行时不 soft_reset → 实际超时=(period-counter) | WDT-04 | Medium | 加 soft_reset |
| `timeout/started` 共享状态无锁 | F-04 | Medium-Low | 关键段加 irqsave |
| 无双重初始化保护 | F-10 | Low | 加 guard |

### 2.3 Round 2 新挖出但**非根因**的隐患

| Finding | 评估 |
|---|---|
| WDT-02 keepalive 写错寄存器（`0x04` dev_version vs `0x0C` dev_status） | 需核实布局；但板端 APB WDT 被喂稳 → key+period 重写已足够喂狗，status clear 非必需。改时一并修正或删除该步 |
| WDT-03 keepalive 缺 soft_reset | SDK 每次 feed soft_reset，但板端未挂 → BK7258 上 key+period 重写即喂狗。修复时对齐 SDK 加 soft_reset |
| F-07 start() soft_reset 未重新上电 | 需独立确认；非当前根因 |

> 这些隐患在"保留手写 APB WDT"前提下需逐一对齐 SDK；若后续 APB 改 SDK 接口则一并消失。

### 2.4 评分（双轮加权）

- L1-3 资源管理：F-01 Critical + F-03 → 重扣
- L1-7 嵌入式：F-01 Critical + WDT-03/F-07 + F-05 → 重扣
- L1-8 设计（独立）：DP-07 -4 → B 级
- **两个 Critical（F-01 重叠计）→ 一票否决封顶 60 → 实际 ~45，NEEDS_FIX**
- 修复 F-01（AON WDT）后即消除 Critical，进 PASS 区

---

## 3. 根因详解

### 3.1 Boot handoff 状态机

```
bootloader:
  start.S:70-84      disarms APB+AON (period=0)
  boot_main.c:193    boot_wdt_init() → arm APB(8s) + AON(8s)   [T0]
  boot_main.c:259    boot_wdt_feed() → 喂 APB only            [最后喂]
  → jump to app

app:
  board_app_initialize():
    procfs mount、DVFS procfs、flash MTD/LittleFS...           [耗时可能数秒]
    line 172: bk7258_wdt_initialize()
      watchdog_register("/dev/watchdog0", APB_lowerhalf)
        → automonitor_start:
            WD_SETTIMEOUT(8000)  → settimeout(8000)
            WD_START             → start()                     [APB 被 NuttX 接管]
        → 此后每 4s WD_KEEPALIVE → keepalive() → 喂 APB        ✅ APB 有人喂
      AON WDT: 无任何代码引用 0x44000600                          ❌ AON 无人喂

[ T0 + 8s ] AON WDT 超时 → 芯片复位 → 回 bootloader → 再 arm → 再 reset
= 无限重启
```

### 3.2 为什么 AON WDT 比其它 init 先到

`bk7258_wdt_initialize()` 在 bringup **第 172 行**，前面已做 procfs mount + DVFS procfs 注册。
但更关键：AON WDT 从 **bootloader T0 就开始倒计时**，到 app 真正站稳并喂上它，已过了
bootloader 全流程 + app early/late initialize 的时间。即使 app 8s 内跑到 line 172 也没用——
**之后**再没人喂 AON（automonitor 只喂 APB）。

---

## 4. 修复方案

### 4.1 核心修复：app 进来**第一时间**关掉 AON WDT

AON WDT 不纳入 NuttX watchdog upper-half（框架单 dog 模型），app 接管后**直接关掉它**，
只保留 APB WDT 由 NuttX automonitor 喂。关狗协议用与 bootloader 已验证的**同一套 key 序列**
（period=0 关狗），不引入 SDK AON WDT 子系统依赖。

**为什么不用 SDK `bk_aon_wdt_stop()`**：
- SDK `bk_aon_wdt_stop()` → `aon_wdt_deinit_common()` → `aon_wdt_hal_stop_aon_wdt()`，本身薄，
  but `aon_wdt_driver.c` 仍 `#include "reset_reason.h"`、`os/mem.h`，且依赖 `CONFIG_SYSTEM_CTRL`。
  为关一个狗把 AON WDT HAL + reset_reason + os_mem 拖进来，违背本阶段"最小修复"原则。
- bootloader `boot_wdt.h:73-95` 已用 `key1+period=0 / key2+period=0` 这套协议 arm 过 AON WDT
  并板端工作；**关狗用同一协议的 period=0 形式**（与 APB `stop()` 现有写法一致），零新增依赖。

### 4.2 修复点位

**`bk7258_wdt.c`**：
1. 新增 AON WDT 常量与关狗 helper（对齐 bootloader `boot_wdt.h`）：
   ```c
   #define BK7258_AON_WDT_BASE   0x44000600u
   #define BK7258_AON_WDT_CTRL   (BK7258_AON_WDT_BASE)        /* ctrl @ base */
   /* key1/key2/period 复用 APB 的定义 */
   static inline void bk7258_aon_wdt_stop(void){
     putreg32(BK7258_WDT_KEY1 << BK7258_WDT_KEY_SHIFT, BK7258_AON_WDT_CTRL);
     putreg32(BK7258_WDT_KEY2 << BK7258_WDT_KEY_SHIFT, BK7258_AON_WDT_CTRL);
   }
   ```
2. `bk7258_wdt_initialize()` **开头最先**调 `bk7258_aon_wdt_stop()`（抢在 automonitor 启动、
   抢在任何可能耗时的操作之前），消除 bootloader 遗留的 AON WDT 倒计时。
3. 顺带修：`watchdog_register` 返回值检查；`settimeout(0)` 拒绝；`settimeout` 运行时加 soft_reset；
   关键段 irqsave；双重初始化 guard。这些在保留手写 APB 前提下做最小对齐。

**`bk7258_bringup.c`**：把 `bk7258_wdt_initialize()` 的调用**前移到 bringup 最开始**（procfs/DVFS/flash 之前），
确保 AON WDT 在最早可能时刻被关掉，给后续 init 消除 AON 超时压力。

**bootloader**：不动（AON WDT 在 bootloader 阶段仍需兜底 cold-init 挂死场景；bootloader 跳 app 前不关狗是合理设计，由 app 接管）。

### 4.3 为什么 APB WDT 保留手写不改 SDK

- 板端已被 automonitor 稳定喂狗（**非根因**）
- SDK `wdt_driver.c` 依赖 `os/os.h`、`reset_reason`、`bk_fake_clock`、`icu_driver`、`power_driver`、
  `sys_driver`、`timer`、`bk_wdt`、`aon_pmu_driver`、`aon_rtc`、`gpio_driver` 全栈——为已工作的 APB WDT
  牵动整条依赖链，违背最小修复原则（见 [[bk7258-sdk-integration-n6a]] / `n6a-sdk-integration-research.md`：
  SDK 引入应按模块增量，先 flash 验证路径，再逐步扩大）
- DP-07 指出的"手写 vs SDK"在本阶段记为已知技术债，**待后续 SDK 集成推进到位后**
  APB WDT 一并切到 `bk_wdt_start/feed/stop`（届时 WDT-02/03/04/F-06/F-07 全部因直调 SDK 而消失）

---

## 5. 验证

2. 烧录：`all-app.bin` @ 0x0（BKFIL/bk_loader，见 [[bk7258-flash-flow-bkfil]]）
3. 板端回归（关键指标：**不再 8s 重启**）：

你说得对，这是我判断上的保守错误。既然你明确要**全面转 SDK**，那 WDT 现在就该用 SDK 接口（`bk_wdt_*` + `bk_aon_wdt_*`）做从头适配，而不是"先手写修 AON，以后再切"。拖到后面反而要重做一遍，还攒技术债。

这正是 N6-A 调研定的方向：模块增量引入 SDK。flash 是第一个，**WDT 现在就该作为第二个**，直接把 `bk_wdt_*` / `bk_aon_wdt_*` 引进来，一次性把 F-02 DP-07 + WDT-02/03/04/F-06/F-07 全部解决，而不是手写修修补补再推翻。

调整方案如下：

## 修正后的方案：WDT 直接用 SDK 接口适配

### 引入的 SDK 源码

从 `$BK_AVDK/cp/middleware/` 拷到 `$CONTEST/board/bk7258_t5ai/sdk/`（与 flash 同一 `sdk/` 目录，增量）：

```
sdk/
├── driver/
│   ├── wdt/
│   │   ├── wdt_driver.c / wdt_driver.h      # bk_wdt_start/feed/stop/driver_init
│   │   └── (cli_wdt_api.c 不需要)
│   ├── aon_wdt/
│   │   ├── aon_wdt_driver.c / aon_wdt_driver.h   # bk_aon_wdt_stop/feed/set_period
│   │   └── bk_aon_wdt.h
│   ├── common/  (已在 flash 阶段拷入，复用)
│   └── sys_ctrl/ (依赖，按编译补)
├── soc/
│   ├── bk7258/hal/
│   │   ├── wdt_ll.c / wdt_ll.h
│   │   ├── aon_wdt_ll.c / aon_wdt_ll.h
│   │   ├── aon_pmu_hal.c   # bk_wdt driver_init 依赖
│   │   └── icu_ll.c        # 时钟门控依赖
│   └── bk7258/soc/
│       ├── wdt_reg.h / wdt_struct.h
│       └── aon_wdt_reg.h
└── include/...
```

### NuttX wrapper（`bk7258_wdt.c` 改为调 SDK）

按 `wdg_pattern.md` 的 lower-half 契约，ops 全部转发到 SDK：

```c
/* start: SDK bk_wdt_start 上电+设period */
static int bk7258_wdt_start(struct watchdog_lowerhalf_s *lower) {
  struct bk7258_wdt_lowerhalf_s *priv = (void *)lower;
  bk_wdt_driver_init();              /* 首次上时钟/初始化 */
  return bk_wdt_start(priv->timeout) == BK_OK ? OK : -EIO;
}

/* keepalive = SDK bk_wdt_feed（内部 soft_reset+key，由此消除 WDT-03） */
static int bk7258_wdt_keepalive(struct watchdog_lowerhalf_s *lower) {
  return bk_wdt_feed() == BK_OK ? OK : -EIO;
}

/* stop = SDK bk_wdt_stop + 关 AON */
static int bk7258_wdt_stop(struct watchdog_lowerhalf_s *lower) {
  bk_wdt_stop();
  bk_aon_wdt_stop();                 /* 消除 F-01 根因 */
  return OK;
}

/* settimeout: 拒绝 0（消除 F-06），运行时 SDK 自动 soft_reset（消除 WDT-04） */
static int bk7258_wdt_settimeout(struct watchdog_lowerhalf_s *lower, uint32_t timeout) {
  if (timeout == 0) return -EINVAL;
  priv->timeout = MIN(timeout, BK7258_WDT_PERIOD_MASK);
  return OK;
}
```

**initialize 里第一时间关 AON WDT**（根因修复）+ register 前初始化：

```c
int bk7258_wdt_initialize(void) {
  static bool s_inited;  if (s_inited) return OK; s_inited = true;   /* F-10 guard */
  bk_aon_wdt_stop();      /* ★根因：立刻关 bootloader 遗留的 AON 狗 */
  priv->ops = &g_bk7258_wdt_ops;
  priv->timeout = BK7258_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS;
  void *h = watchdog_register("/dev/watchdog0", (void *)priv);       /* F-03 检查返回 */
  return h ? OK : -ENOMEM;
}
```

`bk7258_bringup.c` 把 `bk7258_wdt_initialize()` 前移到 bringup 最开始——AON WDT 越早关越好。

### 依赖处理

`wdt_driver.c` 依赖较重（`icu_driver`/`power_driver`/`sys_driver`/`aon_pmu_driver`/`reset_reason`/`bk_fake_clock`）。策略与 flash 一致：**拷最小集 + 桩 + `#ifdef` 裁剪 + `-DCONFIG_FREERTOS=0`**，编译报缺什么补什么，逐层收敛。`bk_aon_wdt_driver.c` 依赖轻（`aon_wdt_hal` + `os_mem` + `reset_reason`）。

### 这套方案一并解决

| 问题 | 消解方式 |
|---|---|
| F-01 AON 无人喂（根因） | `bk7258_wdt_stop` 调 `bk_aon_wdt_stop()` + initialize 先关 |
| F-02 DP-07 重复造轮子 | ops 全转 SDK，删除手写寄存器 |
| F-03 register 返回未检查 | initialize 加检查 |
| F-06 settimeout(0) 关狗 | 加 `==0` 拒绝 |
| WDT-03 keepalive 缺 soft_reset | `bk_wdt_feed` 内部已含 |
| WDT-04 settimeout 运行时不 reset | SDK `bk_wdt_start` 含 reset |
| WDT-02 keepalive 写错寄存器 | 不再手写 status，整段消除 |
| F-07 start soft_reset 未重新上电 | `bk_wdt_start` 内部 `wdt_init_common` 已处理 |
| F-10 双重初始化 | guard |

这些之前手写修要逐个对齐，现在调 SDK 全部一次性消失——这就是你说的"早晚要转，不如现在就转"的价值。

## 4. 修复方案

### 4.1 核心修复：app 进来**第一时间**关掉 AON WDT

AON WDT 不纳入 NuttX watchdog upper-half（框架单 dog 模型），app 接管后**直接关掉它**，
只保留 APB WDT 由 NuttX automonitor 喂。关狗协议用与 bootloader 已验证的**同一套 key 序列**
（period=0 关狗），不引入 SDK AON WDT 子系统依赖。

**为什么不用 SDK `bk_aon_wdt_stop()`**：
- SDK `bk_aon_wdt_stop()` → `aon_wdt_deinit_common()` → `aon_wdt_hal_stop_aon_wdt()`，本身薄，
  but `aon_wdt_driver.c` 仍 `#include "reset_reason.h"`、`os/mem.h`，且依赖 `CONFIG_SYSTEM_CTRL`。
  为关一个狗把 AON WDT HAL + reset_reason + os_mem 拖进来，违背本阶段"最小修复"原则。
- bootloader `boot_wdt.h:73-95` 已用 `key1+period=0 / key2+period=0` 这套协议 arm 过 AON WDT
  并板端工作；**关狗用同一协议的 period=0 形式**（与 APB `stop()` 现有写法一致），零新增依赖。

### 4.2 修复点位

**`bk7258_wdt.c`**：
1. 新增 AON WDT 常量与关狗 helper（对齐 bootloader `boot_wdt.h`）：
   ```c
   #define BK7258_AON_WDT_BASE   0x44000600u
   #define BK7258_AON_WDT_CTRL   (BK7258_AON_WDT_BASE)        /* ctrl @ base */
   /* key1/key2/period 复用 APB 的定义 */
   static inline void bk7258_aon_wdt_stop(void){
     putreg32(BK7258_WDT_KEY1 << BK7258_WDT_KEY_SHIFT, BK7258_AON_WDT_CTRL);
     putreg32(BK7258_WDT_KEY2 << BK7258_WDT_KEY_SHIFT, BK7258_AON_WDT_CTRL);
   }
   ```
2. `bk7258_wdt_initialize()` **开头最先**调 `bk7258_aon_wdt_stop()`（抢在 automonitor 启动、
   抢在任何可能耗时的操作之前），消除 bootloader 遗留的 AON WDT 倒计时。
3. 顺带修：`watchdog_register` 返回值检查；`settimeout(0)` 拒绝；`settimeout` 运行时加 soft_reset；
   关键段 irqsave；双重初始化 guard。这些在保留手写 APB 前提下做最小对齐。

**`bk7258_bringup.c`**：把 `bk7258_wdt_initialize()` 的调用**前移到 bringup 最开始**（procfs/DVFS/flash 之前），
确保 AON WDT 在最早可能时刻被关掉，给后续 init 消除 AON 超时压力。

**bootloader**：不动（AON WDT 在 bootloader 阶段仍需兜底 cold-init 挂死场景；bootloader 跳 app 前不关狗是合理设计，由 app 接管）。

### 4.3 为什么 APB WDT 保留手写不改 SDK

- 板端已被 automonitor 稳定喂狗（**非根因**）
- SDK `wdt_driver.c` 依赖 `os/os.h`、`reset_reason`、`bk_fake_clock`、`icu_driver`、`power_driver`、
  `sys_driver`、`timer`、`bk_wdt`、`aon_pmu_driver`、`aon_rtc`、`gpio_driver` 全栈——为已工作的 APB WDT
  牵动整条依赖链，违背最小修复原则（见 [[bk7258-sdk-integration-n6a]] / `n6a-sdk-integration-research.md`：
  SDK 引入应按模块增量，先 flash 验证路径，再逐步扩大）
- DP-07 指出的"手写 vs SDK"在本阶段记为已知技术债，**待后续 SDK 集成推进到位后**
  APB WDT 一并切到 `bk_wdt_start/feed/stop`（届时 WDT-02/03/04/F-06/F-07 全部因直调 SDK 而消失）

## 4. 修复方案：WDT 全量转 Beken SDK 接口

### 4.1 决策依据

- 早晚全面转 SDK（用户决策），WDT 现在转 = 与 flash 同期增量，**不攒技术债、不重复劳动**
- 一次性清掉：根因 F-01（AON 无人喂）+ 设计债 DP-07（手写寄存器）+ 手写隐患
  WDT-02/03/04、F-06/F-07（见 §4.6）
- 调 SDK 的 `bk_wdt_feed/start/stop` 内部已含 soft_reset + 时钟上电 + key 序列，
  NuttX wrapper 只需薄转发，符合 `wdg_pattern.md` lower-half 契约

### 4.2 引入的 SDK 源码（从 `$BK_AVDK/cp/middleware/` 拷到 `$CONTEST/board/bk7258_t5ai/sdk/`）

与 flash 同一 `sdk/` 目录，增量引入：

```
sdk/
├── driver/
│   ├── wdt/
│   │   ├── wdt_driver.c / wdt_driver.h        # bk_wdt_start/feed/stop/driver_init/deinit
│   │   └── (cli_wdt_api.c 不需要)
│   ├── aon_wdt/
│   │   ├── aon_wdt_driver.c / aon_wdt_driver.h
│   │   └── bk_aon_wdt.h                        # bk_aon_wdt_stop/feed/set_period
│   ├── common/  (flash 阶段已拷，复用)
│   ├── sys_ctrl/  (依赖，按编译补 sys_driver.c/.h)
│   ├── icu/        (icu_driver，wdt_driver_init 依赖)
│   ├── pmu/        (power_driver，时钟上电依赖)
│   └── aon_pmu/    (aon_pmu_driver，wdt rst dev enable)
├── soc/
│   ├── bk7258/hal/
│   │   ├── wdt_ll.c / wdt_ll.h
│   │   ├── aon_wdt_ll.c / aon_wdt_ll.h
│   │   ├── icu_ll.c / icu_ll.h
│   │   ├── aon_pmu_hal.c
│   │   └── (其余按编译报缺补)
│   └── bk7258/soc/
│       ├── wdt_reg.h / wdt_struct.h
│       └── aon_wdt_reg.h
└── include/  (driver/wdt.h、driver/aon_wdt.h、os/、common/ 等最小子集)
```

> **实际引入范围以编译收敛为准**（与 flash 策略一致）：先拷 wdt + aon_wdt 主干，编译报缺
> 哪个头/符号再补，逐层收敛，避免一开始拷一大堆。

### 4.3 NuttX wrapper —— `bk7258_wdt.c` 改为调 SDK（薄转发）

按 `wdg_pattern.md` 的 `struct watchdog_ops_s` 契约，ops 全部转发到 SDK：

```c
#include <driver/wdt.h>          /* SDK: bk_wdt_* */
#include <driver/aon_wdt.h>     /* SDK: bk_aon_wdt_* */

/* start = SDK bk_wdt_start（内部 wdt_init_common 上电 + wdt_ll_set_period soft_reset + key）*/
static int bk7258_wdt_start(struct watchdog_lowerhalf_s *lower) {
  struct bk7258_wdt_lowerhalf_s *priv = (void *)lower;
  if (!bk_wdt_is_driver_inited()) bk_wdt_driver_init();   /* 首次上时钟/初始化 */
  return (bk_wdt_start(priv->timeout) == BK_OK) ? OK : -EIO;
}

/* keepalive = SDK bk_wdt_feed（内部 soft_reset + key，消除 WDT-03）*/
static int bk7258_wdt_keepalive(struct watchdog_lowerhalf_s *lower) {
  return (bk_wdt_feed() == BK_OK) ? OK : -EIO;
}

/* stop = SDK bk_wdt_stop + 关 AON */
static int bk7258_wdt_stop(struct watchdog_lowerhalf_s *lower) {
  bk_wdt_stop();
  bk_aon_wdt_stop();                                 /* 消除 F-01 根因 */
  return OK;
}

/* settimeout: 拒绝 0（消除 F-06）；运行时由 SDK bk_wdt_start 自动 soft_reset（消除 WDT-04）*/
static int bk7258_wdt_settimeout(struct watchdog_lowerhalf_s *lower, uint32_t timeout) {
  struct bk7258_wdt_lowerhalf_s *priv = (void *)lower;
  if (timeout == 0) return -EINVAL;
  priv->timeout = (timeout > BK7258_WDT_PERIOD_MASK) ? BK7258_WDT_PERIOD_MASK : timeout;
  if (priv->started) bk_wdt_start(priv->timeout);     /* SDK 含 soft_reset */
  return OK;
}
```

注册函数（initialize 里**第一时间**关 AON WDT 修根因 + register 返回值检查 + 防重入）：

```c
int bk7258_wdt_initialize(void) {
  static bool s_inited;  if (s_inited) return OK; s_inited = true;   /* F-10 guard */

  bk_aon_wdt_stop();          /* ★根因修复：立刻关 bootloader 遗留的 AON 狗，抢在 automonitor 之前 */
  bk_wdt_driver_init();       /* SDK WDT 驱动初始化（时钟/控制结构） */

  priv->wdt_lh.ops = &g_bk7258_wdt_ops;
  priv->timeout = BK7258_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS;        /* 8000ms，对齐 automonitor TIMEOUT */
  priv->started = false;

  void *h = watchdog_register("/dev/watchdog0", (struct watchdog_lowerhalf_s *)priv);
  return h ? OK : -ENOMEM;                          /* F-03 检查返回 */
}
```

调用时机改造（`bk7258_bringup.c`）：把 `bk7258_wdt_initialize()` **前移到 bringup 最开头**
（procfs / DVFS / flash MTD 之前），AON WDT 越早关越好，消除 bootloader 倒计时压力。
NuttX automonitor 在 register 时自动 `WD_START` APB WDT 并每 4s 喂，APB 路径不变且更稳。

### 4.4 依赖处理（与 flash 同策略）

`wdt_driver.c` 依赖偏重：`os/os.h`、`os/mem.h`、`reset_reason`、`bk_fake_clock`、
`icu_driver`、`power_driver`、`sys_driver`、`aon_pmu_driver`、（可选）`aon_rtc`、`gpio_driver`。
`aon_wdt_driver.c` 依赖轻：`aon_wdt_hal` + `os_mem` + `reset_reason`。

处理：
- **最小集拷入 + 空桩 + `#ifdef` 裁剪 + `-DCONFIG_FREERTOS=0`**（`os_malloc`→`kmm_malloc` 等，
  见 N6-A §3.4 `sdk/os/os_adapt.c`，flash 阶段已在建，复用扩充）
- 编译报未定义符号逐个补/桩（如 `bk_fake_clock`、`bk_get_tick` 用 `clock_systime_ticks` 适配）
- 裁剪不需要的分支：`CONFIG_INT_WDT`/`CONFIG_TASK_WDT` 任务级看门狗（SDK 内部 FreeRTOS 任务
  监控）整体关掉，只保留硬件 WDT 主路径 `bk_wdt_start/feed/stop` + `bk_aon_wdt_*`

### 4.5 不改的部分

- **bootloader**：`boot_wdt.h`/`boot_main.c` 不动。bootloader 阶段 AON WDT 仍需兜底 cold-init
  挂死场景；跳 app 前不关狗是合理设计，由 app `bk7258_wdt_initialize` 接管。
- **defconfig**：`CONFIG_WATCHDOG_AUTOMONITOR=y`/`PING_INTERVAL=4`/`TIMEOUT=8000` 不变
  （automonitor 机制对 lower-half 透明，改 SDK 后仍由它在 register 时启动 APB 喂狗）。
- **`CONFIG_BK7258_WDT`** 仍是芯片 Kconfig 开关，`Make.defs` 改为同时拉 SDK WDT 源码。

### 4.6 此方案一并消除的问题

| 问题 | 消解方式 |
|---|---|
| **F-01 AON 无人喂（重启根因）** | `bk7258_wdt_stop` 调 `bk_aon_wdt_stop()` + initialize 最先关 AON |
| F-02 DP-07 重复造轮子 | ops 全转 SDK，删除手写寄存器/常量 |
| F-03 register 返回未检查 | initialize 加 `h ? OK : -ENOMEM` |
| F-04 共享状态无锁 | SDK 内部原子性 + NuttX 侧不再有跨上下文手写状态（详见 §4.7） |
| F-06 settimeout(0) 关狗 | 加 `==0` 返回 `-EINVAL` |
| F-07 start soft_reset 未重新上电 | `bk_wdt_start` 内部 `wdt_init_common` 已上电 |
| F-10 双重初始化 | `static bool s_inited` guard |
| WDT-02 keepalive 写错寄存器 | 不再手写 status，整段删除 |
| WDT-03 keepalive 缺 soft_reset | `bk_wdt_feed` 内部含 |
| WDT-04 settimeout 运行时不 reset | `bk_wdt_start` 含 soft_reset |

### 4.7 残留与遗留

- **F-04 共享状态无锁**：转 SDK 后 `priv->timeout/started` 仍可能被 automonitor 的 keepalive
  与用户 ioctl settimeout 跨上下文访问。最小处理：`settimeout`/`start`/`stop` 关键段加
  `enter_critical_section()`/`leave_critical_section()`。SDK 侧硬件操作自身原子。
- **F-09 timeleft 恒等于 timeout**：BK7258 APB WDT 无可读计数器，SDK 亦不提供；保留注释说明，
  NuttX automonitor 不依赖 timeleft。无解，可接受。
- **F-05 W1C status 清除**：转 SDK 后该手写段删除，问题自动消失。

你有没有发现sdk是区分ap和cp的 目前BK7258是三核AMP系统架构，CPU0和CPU1,CPU2的软件独立编译，但SDK是一套，所以CPU0和CPU1以及CPU2的部分功能差异需要使用宏区分。

比如TRNG随机数控制器只有一份，使用多核配置时，应用程序需要互斥配置在哪一个系统(CPU0/CPU1/CPU2)中执行。

模块的功能开关CONFIG_TRNG宏默认关闭, 哪个CPU需要, 就在哪个CPU的芯片配置文件上打开。 假设CPU0需要使用TRNG，而CPU1不需要使用，则bk7258.defconfig中的CONFIG_TRNG=y。

在软件代码中，使用CONFIG_TRNG宏隔离调用。 示例如下: CP代码完全独立, 只包含Wi-Fi, BLE和少部分基础外设, 运行在cpu0上

AP代码完全独立, 包含多媒体方案, 客户主要在AP上开发, cpu1和cpu2实现SMP

你这补充非常关键，直接影响 SDK 引入的正确性。我确实没在前面把"AP/CP 三核分编、一套 SDK 用宏区分"这个架构因素纳入考虑——之前看的都是 `cp/middleware/`（CP 路径）。WDT/flash 这类基础外设按你说的属于 **CP 侧（CPU0）**，而 TRNG 这种单份资源靠 `CONFIG_TRNG` 宏互斥分配到某个核。

先确认两件事，避免把 AP/CP 理解错：① BK7258 三核角色对应（CPU0=CP/wifi-ble-基础外设，CPU1/CPU2=AP/多媒体+SMP）② 我们 NuttX 当前跑在哪个核、相当于 AP 还是 CP 配置——这决定用 `cp/` 还是 `ap/` 路径的 SDK，以及 `bk7258.defconfig` 该开哪些 `CONFIG_*`。

架构概述
BK7258由三个core组成,为了更加方便应用层开发, 在原来的架构基础上, Armino SDK设计了新的AP+CP架构, 即SMP(CPU1+CPU2)+CPU0的模式。 其中CPU1+CPU2组成SMP系统, 称为AP, CPU0为单核系统, 称为CP。

明白了，这个架构很关键。让我确认下我们 NuttX 当前跑在哪个核、对应 AP 还是 CP 配置——这决定引入哪个 SDK 路径。

根据记忆里 [[bk7258-nuttx-boot-core-verified]]：
- bootloader 跳转的核是 **CPU0**（bootloader 跳转核）
- N1/N2 板端验证的 NuttX 跑在 **CPU0**
- SDK 分区表 `primary_cp_app`@0x02010000 + `startup_cpu0.c`"app"(master)

而我们设定的 CPU0=CP（单核系统，wifi+ble+基础外设），所以**我们的 NuttX 当前是跑在 CP（CPU0）侧**，应该用 SDK 的 **`cp/` 路径**（这正好是我前面一直在看的 `cp/middleware/`）。这点之前无意中用对了。

Important architectural context I should have given you upfront, please fold into your analysis:

BK7258 is a 3-core AMP SoC with an AP+CP split:
- CP = CPU0 (single core). Runs Wi-Fi, BLE, and a SMALL set of basic peripherals. Our NuttX port runs on CPU0, so we are the CP side.
- AP = CPU1+CPU2 running SMP. Multimedia stack, customer app development lives here.

Key implication for the SDK source I asked you to scope (under /home/lijian/project/armino/bk_avdk_smp/cp/middleware/): we are integrating the CP-side path (cp/), which is exactly what I pointed you at, so that's correct. Good.

The critical part: the SDK is ONE codebase compiled separately per core, and CP-vs-AP (and per-CPU) feature differences are isolated by CONFIG_* macros. Shared single-copy peripherals (like TRNG) must be assigned to exactly one core via the defconfig. So in the wdt_driver.c / aon_wdt_driver.c dependency closure, pay special attention to:
- CONFIG_XXX guards that select CP-only vs AP-only vs specific-CPU features
- Whether WDT / AON_WDT are inherently CP-peripherals (I believe APB WDT and AON WDT are basic peripherals on the CP path, so they should be available on CPU0/CP — confirm)
- Any cross-core (AP/CP) dependencies in the WDT path that would need CONFIG guards or stubs (e.g. does wdt_driver_init touch anything that AP also owns?)

So when answering "which deps must come along vs stub-able", also classify each dependency as: (a) CP-native and safe on CPU0, (b) shared-resource requiring a CONFIG guard / mutual-exclusion, or (c) AP-only path that CP must NOT pull in. And confirm the defconfig knobs we'd set (e.g. CONFIG_WDT=y, CONFIG_AON_WDT=y, leaving AP/media ones off) are the right CP-side switches.

Continue your analysis with this in mind.
